4b2c733e5326a4607920616adf61ce8468f52395 动作: new --- ## 项目学习路线（大纲方法论） # 项目学习手册·大纲规划 Planner ## 角色 你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和项目学习路线设计者。 你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。 你可以使用： - `Read` - `Grep` - `Glob` - 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files` 你不能： - 修改源码 - 写入任何 `.md` 文件 - 输出 JSON 以外的文字 你的唯一产出是一个学习手册大纲 manifest JSON。 --- ## 总目标 为当前项目规划一套「从零开始、由浅入深、结合源码和代码实践」的学习手册。 这套手册会被拆分成多篇 Markdown 讲义，后续 worker 会根据 manifest 逐篇生成。 每篇讲义应该满足： 1. 面向初学者也能读懂。 2. 只讲一个相对独立的主题。 3. 必须结合真实源码。 4. 必须包含一个可操作的代码实践任务。 5. 讲义之间有清晰依赖关系。 --- ## 源码探查顺序 请按以下顺序理解项目，不要一开始就深入细节： 1. 项目说明 - README - docs - examples - tutorials 2. 构建与运行方式 - package.json - Cargo.toml - pyproject.toml - go.mod - pom.xml - Makefile - Dockerfile - CI 配置 3. 项目入口 - CLI 入口 - Web 服务入口 - main 文件 - library export 文件 - examples 入口 4. 目录结构 - src - lib - app - packages - crates - tests 5. 核心流程 - 初始化流程 - 配置加载 - 请求/任务/数据处理主链路 - 插件、扩展、调度、存储等核心机制 6. 测试与示例 - 单元测试 - 集成测试 - benchmark - example usage --- ## 学习路线设计原则 请把学习手册设计成三层： 1. 入门层 beginner 目标：让读者知道项目是什么、怎么运行、目录如何组织、核心入口在哪里。 2. 进阶层 intermediate 目标：让读者理解主要模块、核心调用链、关键数据结构和配置机制。 3. 专家层 advanced 目标：让读者理解扩展点、性能、并发、错误处理、测试、二次开发和架构取舍。 --- ## 讲义拆分规则 - 每篇讲义只解决一个主要问题。 - 每篇讲义包含 2 到 5 个最小模块。 - 每篇讲义必须有一个 `practice_task`，描述读者要完成的代码实践。 - 每篇讲义的源码范围要适中，通常引用 1 到 6 个关键源码文件。 - 大型项目可以拆成 30 篇以上讲义；中型项目 15 到 30 篇；小型项目 8 到 15 篇。 - 不要为了数量硬拆，逻辑优先。 - 第一单元必须帮助读者从零开始，包括项目定位、运行方式、目录结构、入口文件。 - 后续单元再进入核心模块、源码机制、扩展实践。 --- ## mode=full 首次生成大纲时： 1. 阅读项目关键文件。 2. 理解项目定位、技术栈、运行方式和核心模块。 3. 设计从零开始的学习路径。 4. 输出完整 manifest。 5. 所有讲义的 `action` 都必须是 `"new"`。 --- ## mode=incremental 增量更新时： 1. 读取 stdin 中提供的现有 manifest。 2. 阅读项目中已有的 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 讲义目录，理解旧结构。 3. 使用： - `git diff previous_head..current_head` - `git log` - `git show` 分析代码变化。 4. 输出更新后的完整 manifest。 每篇讲义的 `action` 按以下规则设置： - `"keep"` 代码变化不影响这篇讲义，无需重写。 - `"update"` 小范围改动，例如函数重命名、参数调整、局部逻辑变化、链接行号变化。 - `"new"` 新增功能、新增模块、新增重要机制，需要新增讲义。 - `"rebuild"` 架构、主流程、公共接口、核心模型发生重大变化，旧讲义需要重建。 如果某篇旧讲义已经不再适合当前项目结构，可以从 manifest 中移除。 --- ## manifest 输出格式 只输出严格 JSON，不要输出 Markdown，不要输出解释文字。 ```json { "project": "<项目名>", "head": "", "rationale": "中文说明：为什么这样设计学习顺序、单元划分和讲义顺序。", "units": [ { "id": "u1", "title": "单元标题", "level": "beginner", "order": 1, "lectures": [ { "id": "u1-l1", "title": "讲义标题", "order": 1, "filename": "u1-l1-project-overview.md", "level": "beginner", "topic": "本讲义要讲什么，用 1 到 3 句中文说明。", "learning_goals": [ "学习目标 1", "学习目标 2" ], "source_files": [ "README.md", "src/main.ts" ], "minimal_modules": [ "模块 1", "模块 2" ], "practice_task": "本讲义对应的代码实践任务。", "depends_on": [], "action": "new" } ] } ] } ``` --- ## 字段要求 - `project`：项目名。 - `head`：当前 git HEAD。 - `rationale`：中文，一段即可。 - `unit.id`：格式为 `u1`、`u2`、`u3`。 - `lecture.id`：格式为 `u1-l1`、`u1-l2`。 - `filename`： - 必须全局唯一。 - 必须小写。 - 使用连字符。 - 必须以 `.md` 结尾。 - 文件位于 `<项目名>-tutorial/` 目录下。 - `level`： - `"beginner"` - `"intermediate"` - `"advanced"` - `source_files`： - 只能填写你实际读过或确认存在的源码文件。 - 不要编造文件路径。 - `depends_on`： - 使用讲义 id。 - 没有依赖时填写空数组。 - `action`： - full 模式全部为 `"new"`。 - incremental 模式使用 `"keep"`、`"update"`、`"new"`、`"rebuild"`。 --- ## 重要约束 - 只基于真实源码和项目文件规划。 - 不确定的地方写 `"待确认"`。 - 不要编造不存在的模块、命令、接口或源码文件。 - 输出必须是合法 JSON。 ## 完整大纲 ```json { "project": "ground3d-lmm", "rationale": 万问答对，子任务分部件/物体接地、数值测量、空间关系与存在判断三组。架构四组件：SpConvUNet 稀疏编码、超点池化（scatter-mean 把海量点压缩为超点 token）、Qwen3-VL-4B 语言底座（LoRA 微调）、6 层 256 维 Mask2Former 式查询解码器。核心巧思是 `` 机制：回答中 `` 位置的隐状态被复用为分割查询，语言与分割在同一前向内对齐；超点特征并行投影为 `<|point|>` token 与解码器 K/V 两路。项目发布 Joint（3D+RGB）与 3D-only（仅点云）两变体，配置仅差三字段，LoRA rank 与 checkpoint 不匹配时 adapter 会被静默忽略。本讲引入的关键术语：点云、接地（grounding）、超点、LMM、LoRA、特殊 ` 的回答；随后把 prompt 与生成段重组为完整序列做 teacher-forcing 二次前向，取最后一层隐状态、切片对准生成段，交 `get_query_tokens_eval` 全局搜索指称区间得到分割查询。单轮 QA 独立成对话、按三级键写入预测 JSON；多轮为 LLaVA 式滚动历史，点 token 与图像仅第 0 轮注入，记录带 `turn_idx`。推理不做 FPS 聚合；`save_pred_qa_dir` 须显式开启否则写盘报错；JSON 先于分割解码写出且与 mIoU 通道独立；回答保留特殊标记供文本指标，无 `

` 时查询退化为零向量、其 mask 被置为 1e-4。 ### u4-l6 2D 图像分支：Joint 与 3D-only 两种变体 本讲拆解 Ground3D-LMM 的 2D 图像分支两种变体。Joint 变体除点云 token 外，通过 Qwen-VL 原生 message 里的 image 条目注入一帧 RGB 图像，max_pixels 与 min_pixels 经智能缩放把像素钳在固定区间，封顶视觉 token 预算；图像与点 token 策略一致，只在首条 user 消息注入一次。3D-only 无独立代码分支：image_dir 为 None 时 image 条目变 image=None，由 _prepare_messages_data 统一过滤，序列零视觉 token，两变体共享全部解码代码。配置仅差三字段 lora_r、lora_alpha、image_dir；LoRA rank 与 checkpoint 失配会被 strict=False 静默吞掉，模型无声退回基座 Qwen，是重大隐患。训练解码器 Grounded_Decoder_Joint 恒有图，按场景名在双图像目录分流。抽帧工具链由 infos pkl 驱动，产出 image_dir 下的「场景/帧号.jpg」目录树，与解码器的路径拼接构成纯字符串契约。 ### u5-l1 Mask2Former 式查询解码器：逐层前向 本讲剖析查询解码器的逐层前向：共 6 层，每层由「Cross-Attn → Self-Attn → FFN」三件套组成，均为后归一化残差结构、逐场景循环不拼批。核心结论：交叉注意力采用 Mask2Former 式 masked attention，查询只注意上一轮预测掩码内的超点（布尔 attn_mask 约定 True=禁止注意）；自注意力以 ~eye 掩码实现查询隔离，每条查询仅注意自身，防止不同指称目标互相干扰；_forward_head 用 einsum 点积对归一化查询与掩码特征动态打分，sigmoid 低于 0.5 处置为禁止、全禁止行被救援放行并 detach。训练路径把整场景 2560 维语言查询经 query_proj 桥降至 256 维后一次过 6 层，初始 head 加各层 head 共 7 份预测、5 份作辅助深监督；推理路径逐 QA 独立跑完整 6 层，零查询行掩码置 1e-4 哨兵标记无接地，取末层掩码上采样至点级。输出 masks、aux_outputs、original_queries 与 language_losses，交由下一讲损失函数消费。 ### u5-l2 损失函数：语言损失 + 分割损失 本讲剖析 Ground3D-LMM 训练损失如何由预测变成可反传的标量。核心模块三个：Part3dGlammCriterion_v2 组合器是无可训练参数的纯组装者，把解码器预测、sp_gt_masks、language_losses 与 original_queries 分发给两个子损失器并合并字典，输出 text_seg_loss 与 cot_loss 两键，由 mmengine parse_losses 求和；语言与分割的相对权重只能调各子损失器的 loss_weight。CoTCriterion 语言损失是仅落在 assistant 回复 token 上的交叉熵（preprocess_chatml 把提问置 -100），先场景内平均、场景间再 macro-average。TextPrompt_Criterion_Glamm 分割损失对逐超点掩码做 BCE+Dice，依托「

数量契约」行对齐而无需匈牙利匹配；关键概念有有效行过滤（零向量查询且 GT 全 NaN 的行剔除，零查询判定必须在投影前的 original_queries 上做）、dice_scale=4 的 Dice 放大、fix_mean_loss 的无效场景补偿、五层 1/i 递减加权的辅助深监督。GT 侧 sp_gt_seg 逐 QA 生成后拼接为逐场景张量，与查询行、掩码行三方对齐。 ### u5-l3 训练配置与启动：train.sh 背后发生了什么 本讲把唯一训练配置归纳为「模型、数据、优化、起点、钩子」五问清单：数据侧用 ConcatDataset 把 ScanNet 与 ScanNet++ 拼成一条训练流，两个子数据集仅差 data_root 与 ann_file，靠裸文件名契约共享同一 pipeline，并以 _delete_ 重建 dataset、显式关闭 val/test 防继承污染。启动链为 train.sh→dist_train.sh（探测空闲端口后经 torch.distributed.launch 起 4 进程）→tools/train.py→Runner.from_cfg→runner.train()，训练循环是 EpochBasedTrainLoop；--amp 只是把 OptimWrapper 换成 AmpOptimWrapper 壳。优化用 AdamW 加 PolyLR，paramwise_cfg 按参数名子串分层调学习率：'backbone' 是匹配不到任何参数的死键（主干属性名是 unet，实际以基准 lr 训练），'reason' 与 'decoder' 命中语言塔可训练参数（LoRA 与词嵌入两端）。load_from 非严格加载仅初始化 3D 稀疏主干，语言塔由 from_pretrained 独立加载、LoRA 随机起步；--resume 与 load_from 互斥且命令行优先，恢复完整训练状态。 ### u6-l1 分割指标 Part3DGlamm_SegMetric：mIoU 怎么算 本讲解读 `unified_metric.py` 中的 `get_iou` 函数与 `Part3DGlamm_SegMetric` 指标类。核心结论：解码器输出超点级 logits，先 sigmoid 过 `sp_score_thr=0.4` 阈值，再经 `mask[:, superpoints]` 列索引广播成点级掩码；`qa_gt_masks` 与 `qa_pred_masks` 按轮 1:1 对齐，GT 行多则预测补零（诚实惩罚漏检）、行少则预测截断，无 GT 的预测条目仅供可视化。`get_iou` 做两级平均：QA 内先对有效 GT 行（行和大于 0）逐实例取 IoU 均值，再跨 QA 平均；无 `

` 标签任务（如 existence_verification）的 GT 是全 NaN 哨兵，NaN 行和判据自动剔除，无需任务名过滤。`process` 只存每场景 IoU 数组以省内存，`compute_metrics` 拼平后输出 QA Seg mIoU 及严格大于口径的 Precision_half/quarter；`min_num_points`、`id_offset` 等为抄自父类的死参数。 ### u6-l2 评估启动器 eval_ground3d.sh 与配置族 本讲剖析统一评估启动器 eval_ground3d.sh：它把「数据集 × QA 层级 × 子任务」三层循环展开成一串 tools/test.py 调用，经 --cfg-options 覆盖 QA_Generation_Test 的三级旋钮 task_level/task_type/sub_task 与预测输出目录，目录树本身就是按任务归档的结果。核心概念是 LoRA rank 探测（probe_lora_rank）：joint 变体 r=16、3D 变体 r=32，rank 与配置错配时权重被 strict=False 静默丢弃、模型无声退回基座 Qwen，auto 模式靠扫描 lora_A 的 shape[0] 在加载前自动选配置。评估配置族是 2×2 矩阵（scannet/scannetpp × joint/_3d），_3d 版仅覆盖 lora_r、lora_alpha、image_dir 三字段。三级过滤为严格匹配且失败不报错：--levels 非法值在 Bash 侧 LEVEL_MAP 即拦下，--sub_tasks 拼错则静默空跑，权威子任务清单是 ALL_TASKS，长评估前宜 DRYRUN 干跑核对。 ### u6-l3 文本指标：APE、δ@1.25、LLM judge 与 GM-δ 本讲剖析 Ground3D-LMM 的文本评测工具 evaluate_text_metrics.py：它与 mIoU 独立，经 --stages 选择 ape、judge、gmdelta 三阶段。关键概念：任务感知的递归展平（flatten_with_task、gather_samples）把任意嵌套或多轮的预测 JSON 展平为带 _task 标签的扁平样本列表，标签按「meta_info.group → 最近包裹键 → 路径目录名」三级回退；ape 阶段先用文本 LLM 按任务形状抽取数字，再逐对计算 APE 与 δ@1.25，预测缺数被「罚 0」（APE=100%、δ=∞、成功=0），GT 为 0 的对跳过，任务内对 QA 宏观平均、overall 池化平均；judge 阶段用 Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct 对全部任务打 1-10 分，仅聚合幻觉与完整性两维，贪心解码保证可复现，clean_text 定义了但未接线；GM-δ 要求点级掩码 IoU>0.3 且该 QA 全部数值对 δ≤1.25 同时成立，文本与掩码两通道靠「目录镜像＋场景同名＋按位对齐」的纯字符串契约 join（掩码来自推理时 mask dump 落盘的 npy），须显式开启并提供 --mask_dump_dir。核心结论：能量化的数值误差用硬公式与 --selftest 单测覆盖，难量化的幻觉与完整性才交给 LLM 裁判。 ### u6-l4 接地可视化：导出彩色 PLY 点云 本讲打通「被 mIoU 指标丢弃的逐点掩码」到彩色点云的完整链路，覆盖 `predict()` 出口的 mask dump 旁路、离线工具 `export_grounding_ply.py` 与写入器 `grounding_viz.py` 三个模块。核心结论：dump 由环境变量 `MASK_DUMP_DIR` 或配置项 `save_viz_dir` 开启，环境变量优先；逐场景以 object 数组落盘预测与 GT 掩码，按场景名与同名点云 bin 配对；批量评估须用 `--mask-dump` 镜像目录树，防止同场景被子任务静默覆盖。导出分 combine 与 per_qa 两种模式，`--group N` 使颜色在每组内重新起算。染色规则：每个 dump 条目（一条 QA 或多轮的一轮）经行并集后至多占一个区域，单条 QA 内多个指称会被并成同色；颜色按五色调色板循环、重叠处先到先得；`max_frac` 双判据滤除空掩码与全 True 退化掩码（零查询哨兵经阈值所致）；背景乘 `dim_bg` 调暗后写出二进制 PLY。 ### u7-l1 迁移基准：ScanRefer 与 Reason3D 的微调评估 本讲把 Ground3D-LMM 迁移到 ScanRefer 与 Reason3D 两个外部基准，做逐数据集微调后评估（非零样本）。模块一：整场景转换链——共享基类以标注 JSON 的场景键为权威、复用 ScanNet 基座，外部 QA 以 qa_data 整段写入 pkl，v2 规范化借用 reason3d 例程（'scanrefer' 不是合法转换 key）；模块二：超点级 GT 生成——ScanRefer 为实例级指称分割，GT 取 gt_sp_masks_ins 的 object_id 行、答案回显描述原句，Reason3D 为语义级推理分割，GT 取 gt_sp_masks_sem 行、答案为类别名，GT 缺失以 NaN 整行占位；模块三：用 linspace 为每场景确定性抽取 20 张 RGB 视图；模块四：2×2 评估配置矩阵（数据集 × 3D/3D+2D），解码器拆为 Eval_Text 与 Eval_MultiImg，LoRA 统一 r=32，mIoU 基线 38.72/41.30/36.35/41.29，加入 2D 视图稳定涨点，证明架构不限于自建数据；复现需隔离四路输出目录、容忍约一点多方差。 ### u7-l2 二次开发：新增子任务、数据集与替换底座 本讲把 Ground3D-LMM 当作可扩展框架，给出改动地图。新增子任务需过四道关卡：转换侧 ALL_TASKS 白名单、qa_keys 的 GT 分派约定、评估旋钮严格匹配、文本指标名单，漏改均为静默失败；无 `

` 的纯文本任务靠 NaN 哨兵零成本接入。新增数据集遵循「三件套」：Converter（继承共享基类、仅覆盖两个钩子）、Transform（超点 GT 生成器 + QA 采样器）、复用数据集类与 eval 配置，凭裸文件名契约免改模型。替换底座由 base_model 驱动五个分支点，分前向重写式（qwen2_5_vl，弃视觉塔）与钩子叠加式（qwen3_vl，支持 Joint）两条路线，新底座宜抄钩子式。LoRA 旋钮 lora_type/lora_r/lora_alpha 控注入范围、容量与缩放 α/r；max_point_tokens 仅限语言侧 token，训练超限时由零参数 FPS 聚合压缩，推理不聚合。哲学：契约优先、拷贝改优先；须分层干跑验证以防静默失败。 --- ## 本讲义规格 - id: u7-l3 - 文件名: u7-l3-architecture-tradeoffs.md - 写入路径: ground3d-lmm-tutorial/u7-l3-architecture-tradeoffs.md - 标题: 架构取舍与总结：设计决策回顾 - 学习阶段: advanced - 主题: 回顾关键设计取舍：超点 token 化的效率、 隐状态复用为分割查询、LoRA 而非全参微调、生成后再前向的精度考量，并与 UniSeg3D/Mask2Former 对比。 - 学习目标: 论证超点池化相对逐点 token 的效率优势；分析一次生成 + 二次前向取隐状态的代价与动机；评价 Joint 与 3D-only 变体的精度/成本权衡 - 应覆盖的最小模块: 超点 vs 逐点 token 的取舍， 查询机制 vs 专用分割头，joint vs 3D-only 权衡，与 UniSeg3D/Mask2Former 的继承关系 - 关键源码: README.md，uniseg3d/query_decoder.py，uniseg3d/uniseg3d.py，uniseg3d/point_qwen3_vl.py - 代码实践任务: 由 worker 根据主题和源码自行设计 - 依赖讲义: u7-l2 --- ## 任务 请按照 worker prompt 生成这一篇讲义。 要求： 1. 只生成 `ground3d-lmm-tutorial/u7-l3-architecture-tradeoffs.md` 这一个文件。 2. 必须结合真实源码。 3. 必须包含代码实践。 4. 必须使用永久链接引用源码。 5. new/rebuild 模式下从零写入。 6. update 模式下先读取旧文件，再结合 diff 更新。 7. 不要修改源码。 8. 不要写其他文件。 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖的最小模块。

万问答对，子任务分部件/物体接地、数值测量、空间关系与存在判断三组。架构四组件：SpConvUNet 稀疏编码、超点池化（scatter-mean 把海量点压缩为超点 token）、Qwen3-VL-4B 语言底座（LoRA 微调）、6 层 256 维 Mask2Former 式查询解码器。核心巧思是 `` 机制：回答中 `` 位置的隐状态被复用为分割查询，语言与分割在同一前向内对齐；超点特征并行投影为 `<|point|>` token 与解码器 K/V 两路。项目发布 Joint（3D+RGB）与 3D-only（仅点云）两变体，配置仅差三字段，LoRA rank 与 checkpoint 不匹配时 adapter 会被静默忽略。本讲引入的关键术语：点云、接地（grounding）、超点、LMM、LoRA、特殊 token（`<|point|>` 与 ``）、OpenMMLab 配置注册机制。 ### u1-l2 环境搭建：OpenMMLab 栈与 MinkowskiEngine 安装 本讲覆盖四个最小模块：conda 环境与依赖清单、mmcv 源码编译、MinkowskiEngine 源码编译、本包安装与依赖验证。核心结论：Ground3D-LMM 同时依赖 OpenMMLab 四层栈（mmengine→mmcv→mmdet→mmdet3d）、稀疏卷积库 spconv 与 MinkowskiEngine、以及 LLM 栈（transformers/peft），含 CUDA 算子的包必须与 PyTorch 版本、CUDA 工具链、GPU 架构三方对齐，官方锁定 torch2.4.1+cu118；environment.yml 刻意不完整，mmcv/mmdet3d/MinkowskiEngine 须按 Option B 手动源码补装，要点为关闭构建隔离、setuptools<70、ME 从 master 分支编译。本讲引入的关键术语：构建隔离、稀疏卷积、ME 的稀疏批组装与坐标量化（后续超点池化的基础设施）、LoRA/peft、editable 安装。验证方法论是以 import uniseg3d 成功为准而非文档清单，可暴露文档未列的隐藏依赖。 ### u1-l3 仓库结构与 OpenMMLab 注册机制 本讲梳理仓库分层与 OpenMMLab 注册机制。仓库为插件式：configs/ 只写声明，uniseg3d/ 只写实现，tools/ 仅 train.py 与 test.py 构建 Runner，data/ 由用户填充。「注册表」把配置中的 type 字符串映射为真实类：custom_imports 触发导入 uniseg3d，靠 import 副作用执行各模块顶层 register_module 完成注册；注册名默认即类名，尾下划线为继承上游的改版类。mmengine Config 支持 _base_ 跨包继承、递归覆盖与 _delete_ 重建，_3d 变体仅覆盖 3 个字段即成完整配置；--cfg-options 点路径数字即列表下标。 ### u1-l4 快速上手：用预训练权重跑一次接地推理 本讲以复现 README 快速上手为主线，覆盖三个模块：tools/test.py 执行主线、评估配置的任务切换旋钮、预测 JSON 产物结构。核心结论：test.py 是 mmdet3d 通用测试入口，不含任何模型特有逻辑，配置驱动、CLI 优先——`--cfg-options` 按点路径合并进配置（数字即列表下标），checkpoint 位置参数无条件覆盖 `load_from`。评估任务由 `QA_Generation_Test` 的三层旋钮 `task_level`/`task_type`/`sub_task` 决定，None 表示该层不过滤，过滤是严格匹配、拼错静默为空；点路径 `pipeline.2.transforms.2` 的两个下标分别指向 `MultiScaleFlipAug3D` 与该变换；`save_pred_qa_dir` 开启逐场景文本预测 JSON（question/gt_answer/pred_answer 三字段，多轮加 turn_idx），由解码器在 `infer_reason_eval` 中直接写盘；分割 mIoU 则由 `Part3DGlamm_SegMetric` 聚合，两条输出通道相互独立，JSON 不含掩码且写盘先于分割解码。关键术语：checkpoint、snapshot_download、TestLoop、`

` 接地标记。务实习惯：先零 GPU 干跑配置核对覆盖落点，再跑真推理。 ### u2-l1 Ground3D 数据集结构：从 npy 到 QA JSON 本讲解读 Ground3D 数据集的原始组织：每个数据源分三大块——processed_data 存每帧四类逐点对齐的 npy（vert 为 N×6 的 XYZ+RGB 点云，sp/part/object 三类 label 均为长度 N 的实例标签，是实例而非类别）；refined_qa_data 按 part_qa、object_qa、multiturn_qa 三层组织 QA JSON，单轮嵌套结构为「条目 id → 任务名 → 问答列表」，任务名共 9 类（常量 ALL_TASKS，以代码为准）；train/val 划分只认 txt 清单。核心规则：vert.npy 是帧存在的标志，帧 ID 为「场景_frame_序号」；转换时标签统一 int64 写裸 .bin；展平阶段做第一道清洗——跳过统计键与未知任务、给问题补 （单轮无条件、多轮看答案），产出的三个键即评估旋钮 task_level 的取值，为下一讲 create_data.py 的格式转换铺垫。 ### u2-l2 数据转换：create_data.py 生成 infos.pkl 本讲讲解 Ground3D 数据转换链路：create_data.py 是薄入口，按 --dataset 分发、以 --extra-tag 决定 pkl 文件名；Part3dGlammData 以 split txt 清单为唯一权威、扫 vert.npy 定帧，无 QA 的帧整帧丢弃；_flatten_qa_data 把按条目嵌套的 QA 压成按任务索引的字典，并过滤 ALL_TASKS 之外的任务，单轮 QA 无条件补 占位符、多轮仅当答案含 才补；update_pkl_infos 做 v1→v2 规范化并原地覆盖同一 pkl，路径削成裸文件名、目录交由配置的 data_prefix 运行时拼接，qa_data 原样搬运。dtype 契约：npy 写成裸 .bin，object/part mask 强制 int64，super_points 原样搬运而读端统一按 int64 读回，故源 npy 的 dtype 是隐含契约，自制数据集最易在此踩坑。 ### u2-l3 数据集类与点云/标注加载 本讲打通「pkl 裸文件名 → 磁盘文件 → 内存」的加载链。data_prefix 四键（pts、sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask、pts_object_mask）在运行时与 data_root 拼出完整路径，pkl 字段、前缀键、磁盘目录三者必须两两对齐——这是「裸文件名契约」，使数据可迁移、ScanNet 与 ScanNet++ 可共用 pkl。Part3DGlamm_Dataset.parse_data_info 对父类 ScanNetSegDataset 只做增量：补超点（必填，缺键即崩）与部件/物体 mask 路径（可选）、透传 qa_data、从 lidar_path 提取 scene_name、场景采样改为恒等。LoadAnnotations3D_ 通过重写 _load_masks_3d 实现多态替换，统一按 int64 读四类 mask 写入 results（sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask 等），缺失置 None 兜底并同步 eval_ann_info 供评估用。NormalizePointsColor_ 将 RGB 归一化到 [-1,1]。mask 须先于几何增强加载，靠逐点索引对齐维持点与标签的对应；产出的各键是下一讲超点级 GT 生成与 QA 采样的输入。 ### u2-l4 QA 采样与超点标注生成（QA_Generation_v2） 本讲补全数据管线最后一公里。AddSuperPointAnnotations_Part3DGlamm 用 one-hot 加 scatter-mean 再二值化的多数投票，把逐点 part/object mask 聚合成（实例数， 超点数）的超点级 GT 表，并维护原始 ID 参照表，小实例可能整行全 0。QA_Generation_v2 把三层嵌套 QA 展平后随机采样 num_qa 条：多轮对话拆成独立单轮，每条打上 qa_keys/qa_type 标签。核心是形状契约：答案中

标签个数（封顶 2）严格决定该条 QA 的 GT 形状 (num_p_tags, 超点数)，取不到有效 mask 的行用 NaN 占位而非删除，解码器与损失侧均识别并跳过 NaN，永不交付错位 GT。ElasticTransfrom 只生成加噪的体素坐标副本 elastic_coords，不改点也不改任何标签。产出 selected_qa_data 与 sp_gt_seg 逐索引对应，交由下一讲打包。 ### u2-l5 打包与预处理：从 pipeline 到 batch_inputs_dict 本讲是单元2（数据侧）收官：results 字典经 Pack3DDetInputs_Part_Glamm 打包、pseudo_collate 组批、Det3DDataPreprocessor_ 组装，最终成为 loss() 的 batch_inputs_dict 与 batch_data_samples 两个参数。核心结论：数据流分两条物理隔离通道——前向输入走 inputs（训练配置下仅 points、elastic_coords、scene_name、selected_qa_data 四键），监督信号走 data_samples（gt_pts_seg 装 sp_pts_mask 与逐 QA 索引对应的 sp_gt_seg 张量列表）；Pack 按四类键组路由表（INPUTS/SEG/实例键组）分拣，实际打包键＝配置白名单∩results 现有键，未登记新键抛 NotImplementedError，dict/str 列表原样保留以免 QA 文本被 to_tensor 破坏。pseudo_collate 只按位装箱、不堆叠张量，故各值均为按样本的列表，loss() 需用 superpoint_bias/batch_offsets 将各场景超点编号全局化，两条通道最终在 criterion 处汇合。 ### u3-l1 模型主入口 Grounded_LMM_main：init/loss/predict 本讲是 3D 侧入口，解析 Grounded_LMM_main 的三个模块：`__init__` 组件构建、loss() 训练链路、predict() 推理与掩码落盘。核心结论：该类是纯组装者，经 MODELS.build 构建三大组件——SpConvUNet 稀疏卷积主干、Grounded_Decoder_Joint 解码器（内含 Qwen3-VL）、Part3dGlammCriterion_v2 组合损失器；query_thr、set_query_mask、pred_iou 等是继承自 UniSeg3D 的死开关，故训练需 find_unused_parameters=True。loss() 用 tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

万问答对，子任务分部件/物体接地、数值测量、空间关系与存在判断三组。架构四组件：SpConvUNet 稀疏编码、超点池化（scatter-mean 把海量点压缩为超点 token）、Qwen3-VL-4B 语言底座（LoRA 微调）、6 层 256 维 Mask2Former 式查询解码器。核心巧思是 `` 机制：回答中 `` 位置的隐状态被复用为分割查询，语言与分割在同一前向内对齐；超点特征并行投影为 `<|point|>` token 与解码器 K/V 两路。项目发布 Joint（3D+RGB）与 3D-only（仅点云）两变体，配置仅差三字段，LoRA rank 与 checkpoint 不匹配时 adapter 会被静默忽略。本讲引入的关键术语：点云、接地（grounding）、超点、LMM、LoRA、特殊 token（`<|point|>` 与 ``）、OpenMMLab 配置注册机制。 ### u1-l2 环境搭建：OpenMMLab 栈与 MinkowskiEngine 安装 本讲覆盖四个最小模块：conda 环境与依赖清单、mmcv 源码编译、MinkowskiEngine 源码编译、本包安装与依赖验证。核心结论：Ground3D-LMM 同时依赖 OpenMMLab 四层栈（mmengine→mmcv→mmdet→mmdet3d）、稀疏卷积库 spconv 与 MinkowskiEngine、以及 LLM 栈（transformers/peft），含 CUDA 算子的包必须与 PyTorch 版本、CUDA 工具链、GPU 架构三方对齐，官方锁定 torch2.4.1+cu118；environment.yml 刻意不完整，mmcv/mmdet3d/MinkowskiEngine 须按 Option B 手动源码补装，要点为关闭构建隔离、setuptools<70、ME 从 master 分支编译。本讲引入的关键术语：构建隔离、稀疏卷积、ME 的稀疏批组装与坐标量化（后续超点池化的基础设施）、LoRA/peft、editable 安装。验证方法论是以 import uniseg3d 成功为准而非文档清单，可暴露文档未列的隐藏依赖。 ### u1-l3 仓库结构与 OpenMMLab 注册机制 本讲梳理仓库分层与 OpenMMLab 注册机制。仓库为插件式：configs/ 只写声明，uniseg3d/ 只写实现，tools/ 仅 train.py 与 test.py 构建 Runner，data/ 由用户填充。「注册表」把配置中的 type 字符串映射为真实类：custom_imports 触发导入 uniseg3d，靠 import 副作用执行各模块顶层 register_module 完成注册；注册名默认即类名，尾下划线为继承上游的改版类。mmengine Config 支持 _base_ 跨包继承、递归覆盖与 _delete_ 重建，_3d 变体仅覆盖 3 个字段即成完整配置；--cfg-options 点路径数字即列表下标。 ### u1-l4 快速上手：用预训练权重跑一次接地推理 本讲以复现 README 快速上手为主线，覆盖三个模块：tools/test.py 执行主线、评估配置的任务切换旋钮、预测 JSON 产物结构。核心结论：test.py 是 mmdet3d 通用测试入口，不含任何模型特有逻辑，配置驱动、CLI 优先——`--cfg-options` 按点路径合并进配置（数字即列表下标），checkpoint 位置参数无条件覆盖 `load_from`。评估任务由 `QA_Generation_Test` 的三层旋钮 `task_level`/`task_type`/`sub_task` 决定，None 表示该层不过滤，过滤是严格匹配、拼错静默为空；点路径 `pipeline.2.transforms.2` 的两个下标分别指向 `MultiScaleFlipAug3D` 与该变换；`save_pred_qa_dir` 开启逐场景文本预测 JSON（question/gt_answer/pred_answer 三字段，多轮加 turn_idx），由解码器在 `infer_reason_eval` 中直接写盘；分割 mIoU 则由 `Part3DGlamm_SegMetric` 聚合，两条输出通道相互独立，JSON 不含掩码且写盘先于分割解码。关键术语：checkpoint、snapshot_download、TestLoop、`

` 接地标记。务实习惯：先零 GPU 干跑配置核对覆盖落点，再跑真推理。 ### u2-l1 Ground3D 数据集结构：从 npy 到 QA JSON 本讲解读 Ground3D 数据集的原始组织：每个数据源分三大块——processed_data 存每帧四类逐点对齐的 npy（vert 为 N×6 的 XYZ+RGB 点云，sp/part/object 三类 label 均为长度 N 的实例标签，是实例而非类别）；refined_qa_data 按 part_qa、object_qa、multiturn_qa 三层组织 QA JSON，单轮嵌套结构为「条目 id → 任务名 → 问答列表」，任务名共 9 类（常量 ALL_TASKS，以代码为准）；train/val 划分只认 txt 清单。核心规则：vert.npy 是帧存在的标志，帧 ID 为「场景_frame_序号」；转换时标签统一 int64 写裸 .bin；展平阶段做第一道清洗——跳过统计键与未知任务、给问题补 （单轮无条件、多轮看答案），产出的三个键即评估旋钮 task_level 的取值，为下一讲 create_data.py 的格式转换铺垫。 ### u2-l2 数据转换：create_data.py 生成 infos.pkl 本讲讲解 Ground3D 数据转换链路：create_data.py 是薄入口，按 --dataset 分发、以 --extra-tag 决定 pkl 文件名；Part3dGlammData 以 split txt 清单为唯一权威、扫 vert.npy 定帧，无 QA 的帧整帧丢弃；_flatten_qa_data 把按条目嵌套的 QA 压成按任务索引的字典，并过滤 ALL_TASKS 之外的任务，单轮 QA 无条件补 占位符、多轮仅当答案含 才补；update_pkl_infos 做 v1→v2 规范化并原地覆盖同一 pkl，路径削成裸文件名、目录交由配置的 data_prefix 运行时拼接，qa_data 原样搬运。dtype 契约：npy 写成裸 .bin，object/part mask 强制 int64，super_points 原样搬运而读端统一按 int64 读回，故源 npy 的 dtype 是隐含契约，自制数据集最易在此踩坑。 ### u2-l3 数据集类与点云/标注加载 本讲打通「pkl 裸文件名 → 磁盘文件 → 内存」的加载链。data_prefix 四键（pts、sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask、pts_object_mask）在运行时与 data_root 拼出完整路径，pkl 字段、前缀键、磁盘目录三者必须两两对齐——这是「裸文件名契约」，使数据可迁移、ScanNet 与 ScanNet++ 可共用 pkl。Part3DGlamm_Dataset.parse_data_info 对父类 ScanNetSegDataset 只做增量：补超点（必填，缺键即崩）与部件/物体 mask 路径（可选）、透传 qa_data、从 lidar_path 提取 scene_name、场景采样改为恒等。LoadAnnotations3D_ 通过重写 _load_masks_3d 实现多态替换，统一按 int64 读四类 mask 写入 results（sp_pts_mask、pts_part_mask 等），缺失置 None 兜底并同步 eval_ann_info 供评估用。NormalizePointsColor_ 将 RGB 归一化到 [-1,1]。mask 须先于几何增强加载，靠逐点索引对齐维持点与标签的对应；产出的各键是下一讲超点级 GT 生成与 QA 采样的输入。 ### u2-l4 QA 采样与超点标注生成（QA_Generation_v2） 本讲补全数据管线最后一公里。AddSuperPointAnnotations_Part3DGlamm 用 one-hot 加 scatter-mean 再二值化的多数投票，把逐点 part/object mask 聚合成（实例数， 超点数）的超点级 GT 表，并维护原始 ID 参照表，小实例可能整行全 0。QA_Generation_v2 把三层嵌套 QA 展平后随机采样 num_qa 条：多轮对话拆成独立单轮，每条打上 qa_keys/qa_type 标签。核心是形状契约：答案中

标签个数（封顶 2）严格决定该条 QA 的 GT 形状 (num_p_tags, 超点数)，取不到有效 mask 的行用 NaN 占位而非删除，解码器与损失侧均识别并跳过 NaN，永不交付错位 GT。ElasticTransfrom 只生成加噪的体素坐标副本 elastic_coords，不改点也不改任何标签。产出 selected_qa_data 与 sp_gt_seg 逐索引对应，交由下一讲打包。 ### u2-l5 打包与预处理：从 pipeline 到 batch_inputs_dict 本讲是单元2（数据侧）收官：results 字典经 Pack3DDetInputs_Part_Glamm 打包、pseudo_collate 组批、Det3DDataPreprocessor_ 组装，最终成为 loss() 的 batch_inputs_dict 与 迁移基准：ScanRefer 与 Reason3D 的微调评估 本讲把 Ground3D-LMM 迁移到 ScanRefer 与 Reason3D 两个外部基准，做逐数据集微调后评估（非零样本）。模块一：整场景转换链——共享基类以标注 JSON 的场景键为权威、复用 ScanNet 基座，外部 QA 以 qa_data 整段写入 pkl，v2 规范化借用 reason3d 例程（'scanrefer' 不是合法转换 key）；模块二：超点级 GT 生成——ScanRefer 为实例级指称分割，GT 取 gt_sp_masks_ins 的 object_id 行、答案回显描述原句，Reason3D 为语义级推理分割，GT 取 gt_sp_masks_sem 行、答案为类别名，GT 缺失以 NaN 整行占位；模块三：用 linspace 为每场景确定性抽取 20 张 RGB 视图；模块四：2×2 评估配置矩阵（数据集 × 3D/3D+2D），解码器拆为 Eval_Text 与 Eval_MultiImg，LoRA 统一 r=32，mIoU 基线 38.72/41.30/36.35/41.29，加入 2D 视图稳定涨点，证明架构不限于自建数据；复现需隔离四路输出目录、容忍约一点多方差。 ### u7-l2 二次开发：新增子任务、数据集与替换底座 本讲把 Ground3D-LMM 当作可扩展框架，给出改动地图。新增子任务需过四道关卡：转换侧 ALL_TASKS 白名单、qa_keys 的 GT 分派约定、评估旋钮严格匹配、文本指标名单，漏改均为静默失败；无 `

2 3 4 5 # Ground3D-LMM: Fine-Grained 3D Point Grounding
and Spatial Reasoning with LMM 6 7 [![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2607.05493-b31b1b.svg?logo=arxiv&logoColor=white)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05493) 8 [![ECCV 2026](https://img.shields.io/badge/ECCV-2026-4b8bbe.svg)](https://amolharsh.github.io/ground3d-lmm/) 9 [![Project Page](https://img.shields.io/badge/Project-Website-1e6cb6.svg)](https://amolharsh.github.io/ground3d-lmm/) 10 [![Dataset](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dataset-HuggingFace-fcd734.svg?logo=huggingface&logoColor=black)](https://huggingface.co/datasets/amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset) 11 [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache--2.0-4caf50.svg)](LICENSE) 12 [![PyTorch](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-EE4C2C.svg?logo=pytorch&logoColor=white)](https://pytorch.org/) 13 14 --- 15 16 **Amol Harsh · Zongyan Han · Jean Lahoud · Ye Liu · Rao Muhammad Anwer · Hisham Cholakkal · Salman Khan · Fahad Shahbaz Khan** 17 18 **Ground3D-LMM** is a large multimodal model for **fine-grained 3D point grounding** and **spatial reasoning** in indoor scenes. It produces per-point segmentation masks alongside grounded natural-language answers across **8 sub-tasks** on ScanNet and ScanNet++, trained on a **2.47M Q/A pair** dataset. 19 20
21 22 --- 23 24 The architecture combines: 25 - **SpConvUNet** sparse 3D point encoder (from UniSeg3D) 26 - **Qwen3-VL-4B** vision-language model with LoRA fine-tuning 27 - **Mask2Former-style query decoder** (6 layers, 256-d) 28 - **Superpoint pooling** for efficient cross-attention over scenes 29 30 ## 📢 News 31 32 - **[Featured 📣]** *Ground3D-LMM* was featured by [52CV](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/ZH2NctV9Ycg8t4EVui7gIg), a leading Chinese computer-vision community WeChat account. 33 - **[Accepted 🎉]** *Ground3D-LMM: Fine-Grained 3D Point Grounding and Spatial Reasoning with LMM* accepted to **ECCV 2026** (main conference). 34 - **[Released]** Code and Ground3D dataset (2.47M Q/A pairs) released on Hugging Face. 35 36 ## 🏗️ Architecture 37 38 ![Ground3D-LMM architecture](images/method.png) 39 40 A 3D scene (XYZ + RGB point cloud) is encoded by **SpConvUNet** into per-point features, which are then pooled over precomputed superpoints to yield `Fp ∈ ℝ^(M × d)`. `Fp` is projected into two spaces in parallel: (i) into the **Qwen3-VL LMM** as `<|point|>` token embeddings alongside the text prompt and optional RGB frame, and (ii) into the **mask decoder** as keys/values for 6 layers of Mask2Former-style Cross-Attn → Self-Attn → FFN. The LMM generates text that includes `` tokens; the hidden state at each `` becomes a refined query, which is dot-producted against per-point features to produce the final segmentation mask. 41 42 ## 🚀 Install 43 44 ```bash 45 conda create -n ground3d python=3.10 -y 46 conda activate ground3d 47 # Follow docs/INSTALL.md for the OpenMMLab stack + MinkowskiEngine (source builds), 48 # then install this package: 49 pip install -e . 50 ``` 51 52 > **Heads-up:** `conda env create -f environment.yml` does **not** fully work on its own — 53 > `mmcv==2.1.0` has no prebuilt wheel for torch 2.4.1 (needs a source build with an older 54 > `setuptools` + `--no-build-isolation`), and **MinkowskiEngine 0.5.4** must be compiled 55 > from source. Follow [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md) **Option B** for the verified, 56 > step-by-step install, troubleshooting, and tested environment details. 57 58 **Tested**: Ubuntu 20.04 · Python 3.10 · PyTorch 2.4.1 · CUDA 11.8 · A100 80GB / RTX 3090. 59 60 ## ⚡ Quick Start with HuggingFace 61 62 ### Download the dataset 63 ```python 64 from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download 65 66 # Annotations only (~3 GB) for exploration 67 data_root = snapshot_download( 68 repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset", 69 repo_type="dataset", 70 allow_patterns=["*/refined_qa_data/*", "*/part_ground3d_*.txt", "README.md"], 71 ) 72 73 # Full dataset (~150 GB) for training 74 # data_root = snapshot_download(repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset", repo_type="dataset") 75 ``` 76 77 ### Download a pretrained checkpoint 78 ```python 79 from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download 80 81 # Joint variant — uses 3D point cloud + aligned RGB frames (main paper result) 82 ckpt_dir = snapshot_download(repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint") 83 84 # Or the point-only variant — uses 3D points only (no RGB frames needed) 85 # ckpt_dir = snapshot_download(repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D") 86 ``` 87 88 ### Run inference (single config-driven invocation) 89 90 Each released checkpoint has a matching eval config — the Joint (3D + 2D) variant uses 91 `ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py` (LoRA r=16, RGB frames on), and the 3D-only variant 92 uses `ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet_3d.py` (LoRA r=32, no RGB frames). The `_3d` config 93 inherits from the joint one and only overrides those three fields. 94 95 ```bash 96 # --- Joint (3D + 2D) — main paper result --- 97 CKPT="$(huggingface-cli download amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint --quiet)/pytorch_model.pth" 98 CONFIG=configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py 99 100 # --- Or, 3D-only --- 101 # CKPT="$(huggingface-cli download amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D --quiet)/pytorch_model.pth" 102 # CONFIG=configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet_3d.py 103 104 PYTHONPATH=. python tools/test.py \ 105 "$CONFIG" "$CKPT" \ 106 --work-dir work_dirs/quickstart \ 107 --cfg-options \ 108 "model.decoder.save_pred_qa_dir=work_dirs/quickstart/preds" \ 109 "test_dataloader.dataset.pipeline.2.transforms.2.task_level=part_qa_data" \ 110 "test_dataloader.dataset.pipeline.2.transforms.2.task_type=qa_data" \ 111 "test_dataloader.dataset.pipeline.2.transforms.2.sub_task=scale_estimation" 112 ``` 113 114 This runs inference for the `scale_estimation` sub-task on `part_qa_data` and writes: 115 - Per-scene predictions to `work_dirs/quickstart/preds/{scene}.json` 116 - Segmentation mIoU to stdout 117 118 > For batched evaluation across sub-tasks or both datasets, `bash eval_ground3d.sh` auto-detects 119 > the variant from the checkpoint's LoRA rank and picks the matching config — see the 120 > [Evaluation](#-evaluation) section. 121 122 ## 📊 Ground3D Dataset 123 124 Total **2,475,307 Q/A pairs** spanning 8 sub-tasks across ScanNet and ScanNet++ scenes. 125 126 | Source | Train scenes | Val scenes | Object QA | Part QA | Multi-turn | Total | 127 |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| 128 | ScanNet | 1,433 | 80 | 655,760 | 909,905 | 62,064 | 1,627,729 | 129 | ScanNet++ | 857 | 48 | 339,396 | 498,399 | 9,783 | 847,578 | 130 | **Total** | **2,290** | **128** | **995,156** | **1,408,304** | **71,847** | **2,475,307** | 131 132 > Not every ScanNet++ scene could be used: many scenes in the ScanNet++ release are missing the depth 133 > or mesh files our pipeline needs, and a few lost their Q/A during our VLM-based verification stage. 134 > The scene count here may therefore differ slightly from the paper, since some scenes were listed but 135 > held no Q/A and have been removed. **The total number of Q/A pairs is unchanged and matches the paper.** 136 137 ### Sub-tasks 138 1. `functional_part_grounding` 139 2. `functional_object_grounding` 140 3. `scale_estimation` 141 4. `grounded_dimension_reasoning` 142 5. `relative_depth_forward` 143 6. `existence_verification` 144 7. `scale_comparison_size` 145 8. `distance_estimation` 146 9. `relative_position_forward_reasoning` 147 148 Full dataset schema, Q/A JSON layout, and per-file specifications: see the [dataset card on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset). 149 150 ### Prepare the data (download → convert) 151 152 **Step 1 — download** from Hugging Face. Each source (`scannet`, `scannetpp`) ships 153 the raw per-frame arrays plus QA JSON and split lists: 154 155 ``` 156 data/scannet/ 157 ├── processed_data//frame__vert.npy # XYZ+RGB points (load_dim=6) 158 │ frame__sp_label.npy # superpoint ids 159 │ frame__part_label.npy # per-point part labels 160 │ frame__object_label.npy # per-point object labels 161 ├── refined_qa_data/{part_qa,object_qa,multiturn_qa}//... 162 └── part_ground3d_{train,val}.txt # scene split lists 163 ``` 164 165 **Step 2 — convert** the raw `.npy` into the flat `.bin` files and the `infos.pkl` 166 the configs actually consume: 167 168 ```bash 169 python tools/create_data.py --dataset part3d_glamm \ 170 --root-path data/scannet \ 171 --out-dir data/scannet \ 172 --qa_data_dir data/scannet/refined_qa_data 173 ``` 174 175 **ScanNet++** uses the identical layout — just swap the paths (the converter is dataset-agnostic; 176 the ScanNet++ config reuses `data/scannet/scannet_cls_embedding.pth`): 177 178 ```bash 179 python tools/create_data.py --dataset part3d_glamm \ 180 --root-path data/scannetpp \ 181 --out-dir data/scannetpp \ 182 --qa_data_dir data/scannetpp/refined_qa_data 183 ``` 184 185 Resulting layout (what the configs load via `ann_file` + `data_prefix`): 186 187 ``` 188 data/scannet/ 189 ├── points/ super_points/ part_mask/ object_mask/ (_frame_.bin) 190 ├── part3d_glamm_infos_train.pkl 191 ├── part3d_glamm_infos_val.pkl 192 └── scannet_cls_embedding.pth (shipped in this repo) 193 ``` 194 195 > **Joint model only:** the config's `model.decoder.image_dir` expects RGB frames at 196 > `data/scannet/frame_images//.jpg`. These are ScanNet / ScanNet++ images and are 197 > **not redistributable** (so they are not on Hugging Face). Download the raw datasets and extract 198 > the frames each split needs by following **[docs/DATA_IMAGES.md](docs/DATA_IMAGES.md)** 199 > (`tools/build_frame_images.py` does it straight from the `.pkl`). Or use the **3D-only** 200 > checkpoint, which needs no images (`model.decoder.image_dir=None`). 201 202 ## 🤗 Model Zoo 203 204 | Model | Modality | LoRA (r / α) | Eval config | Checkpoint | 205 |---|---|---|---|---| 206 | Ground3D-LMM-4B (Joint) | 3D points + RGB frames | 16 / 32 | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_{scannet,scannetpp}.py` | [🤗 Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint](https://huggingface.co/amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint) — main paper result | 207 | Ground3D-LMM-4B (3D-only) | 3D points only | 32 / 64 | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_{scannet,scannetpp}_3d.py` | [🤗 Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D](https://huggingface.co/amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D) — no RGB frames required | 208 209 Both checkpoints use **Qwen3-VL-4B** as the LLM backbone (4.47B params, ~400M LoRA-trainable). 210 The two variants have different LoRA ranks, so each ships with its own eval config; the config 211 inheritance keeps the diff between them tiny (`lora_r`, `lora_alpha`, `image_dir`). If you're 212 running through `eval_ground3d.sh`, the launcher probes the checkpoint's LoRA rank and picks 213 the matching config automatically — no manual switch needed. 214 215 ## 🏋️ Training 216 217 ### Prepare data 218 1. Download the dataset and arrange under `data/scannet/` and `data/scannetpp/` (see [Local data layout](#local-data-layout)) 219 2. Download pretrained sparse-conv weights into `work_dirs/pretrained/`: 220 - `sstnet_scannet.pth` — used as the point-encoder initialization 221 3. The Qwen3-VL-4B base model will be downloaded automatically by `transformers`. To use a local copy, override via `--cfg-options model.decoder.qwen_model_path=/path/to/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct` 222 223 ### Launch training (4 GPUs, LoRA fine-tuning) 224 ```bash 225 bash train.sh 226 ``` 227 228 This launches `configs/ground3dlmm_train.py` on GPUs 0-3 via `torch.distributed.launch`. Checkpoints are saved to `work_dirs/ground3dlmm/epoch_*.pth`. 229 230 ### Customize the training run 231 Common arguments to edit in `configs/ground3dlmm_train.py`: 232 233 | Field | Default | Purpose | 234 |---|---|---| 235 | `model.decoder.qwen_model_path` | `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct` | Path or HF id of the LLM | 236 | `model.decoder.lora_r`, `lora_alpha` | 16, 32 | LoRA rank and scaling | 237 | `model.decoder.max_point_tokens` | 2000 | Max superpoint tokens fed to LLM | 238 | `train_dataloader.batch_size` | 1 | Per-GPU batch size | 239 | `optim_wrapper.optimizer.lr` | 1e-4 | Base learning rate | 240 | `epoch` | 10 | Total training epochs | 241 | `load_from` | `work_dirs/pretrained/sstnet_scannet.pth` | Backbone init | 242 243 ## 📈 Evaluation 244 245 The paper reports **three categories of metrics**. Full evaluation is a 3-step pipeline: 246 247 ### Step 1 — Run inference (segmentation mIoU + per-scene predictions) 248 249 One launcher, fully argument-driven — pick the dataset / task levels / sub-tasks with flags: 250 ```bash 251 bash eval_ground3d.sh --checkpoint work_dirs/ground3dlmm/pytorch_model.pth # default: scannet, part+object, all sub-tasks 252 253 # choose exactly what to run: 254 bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset all --levels all # both datasets, part+object+multi_turn 255 bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset scannet --levels part,object --sub_tasks distance_estimation,scale_estimation 256 bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset scannetpp --levels multi_turn 257 bash eval_ground3d.sh --help # full option list (+ --gpus, --out-root, --mask-dump) 258 ``` 259 `--dataset` = `scannet`|`scannetpp`|`all`; `--levels` = any of `part,object,multi_turn` (or `all`); 260 `--sub_tasks` = `all` or a comma list. `--variant` = `joint`|`3d`|`auto` (default `auto`): the launcher 261 inspects the checkpoint's LoRA rank (`r=16` → joint, `r=32` → 3D-only) and picks the matching config, 262 so the Joint and 3D-only weights just work with the same command. Pass `--variant` explicitly to 263 override. The old names `eval_ground3d_{scannet,scannetpp,all}.sh` still work — they're thin wrappers 264 that pass flags through. Outputs: 265 - **Segmentation mIoU** (printed per sub-task) 266 - Per-scene prediction JSONs in `val_outputs_joint/{scannet,scannetpp}/pred_qa_data_val/...` 267 268 > Add `--mask-dump ` to also dump per-QA masks (needed for the **GM-δ** stage below, and used by 269 > the grounding visualization). 270 271 `tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py` runs **two independent stages** — pick what you need via `--stages` 272 (`ape`, `judge`, or `all`). The `--input` dir is searched **recursively**, nested / multi-turn 273 prediction JSONs are flattened automatically, and each sample is tagged with its task. `ape` uses a 274 text LLM (`--llm_model_path`, default `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507`) to extract numbers; `judge` uses 275 the paper's VL judge (`--judge_model_path`, default `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`). Both run via 276 **HuggingFace transformers**. Sanity-check the numeric math with 277 `python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --selftest`. 278 279 ### Step 2 — `ape` : numeric APE + δ@1.25 (the 4 numeric tasks only) 280 ```bash 281 python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --input val_outputs_joint/scannet/pred_qa_data_val \ 282 --output eval_results/scannet_ape.json --stages ape \ 283 --llm_model_path Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 --gpus 0,1,2,3 284 ``` 285 Runs **only** on `distance_estimation`, `grounded_dimension_reasoning`, `scale_estimation`, 286 `scale_comparison_size`. The LLM extracts the scalar(s) in metres (per-task JSON shape; a missing 287 prediction → `0.0` so it is penalised), then reports **APE** `|ŝ−s|/s×100%` and **δ@1.25** success 288 (`δ = max(ŝ/s, s/ŝ) ≤ 1.25`; GT==0 pairs skipped; mean over pairs, then macro-averaged per task). 289 290 ### Step 3 — `judge` : LLM judge — Hallucination + Completeness (all tasks) 291 ```bash 292 python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --input val_outputs_joint/scannet/pred_qa_data_val \ 293 --output eval_results/scannet_judge.json --stages judge \ 294 --judge_model_path Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct --gpus 0,1,2,3 295 ``` 296 The Table-4 judge — **Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct** — scores each prediction and reports **Hallucination** 297 and **Completeness** (over all tasks). Run both stages with `--stages all` (the `ape` extractor 298 stays on the text `Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507`). 299 300 ### Step 3b — `gmdelta` : GM-δ (supplementary, opt-in) 301 GM-δ (Grounded-Measurement) counts a prediction correct only when **mask IoU > 0.3 AND δ ≤ 1.25**, on 302 the numeric tasks that also ground. Run the numeric sub-tasks **with `--mask-dump`** (the mask tree 303 mirrors the prediction tree), then **one command auto-iterates all 4 numeric tasks × both datasets**: 304 ```bash 305 # 1. inference for the 4 numeric tasks on both datasets, dumping per-QA masks 306 bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset all --levels part \ 307 --sub_tasks distance_estimation,grounded_dimension_reasoning,scale_estimation,scale_comparison_size \ 308 --mask-dump masks --checkpoint work_dirs/ground3dlmm/pytorch_model.pth 309 310 # 2. GM-δ across all of them in a single run 311 python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages gmdelta \ 312 --input val_outputs_joint --mask_dump_dir masks \ 313 --llm_model_path Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 --gpus 0,1,2,3 --output eval_results/gmdelta.json 314 ``` 315 It reports GM-δ **per (dataset, task)** and **overall**. `--gmdelta_task all` (default) auto-discovers 316 the numeric tasks; pass a single task name to restrict. 317 318 ### Metric provenance (the paper's metrics) 319 320 | Metric | Provided by | Tasks | 321 |---|---|---| 322 | Segmentation mIoU | `tools/test.py` → `Part3DGlamm_SegMetric` | all sub-tasks (over each QA's `` grounding) | 323 | APE & δ@1.25 (LLM-extracted) | `evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages ape` | 4 numeric tasks | 324 | Hallucination + Completeness (LLM judge) | `evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages judge` | all tasks | 325 | GM-δ (IoU>0.3 ∧ δ≤1.25), *supplementary* | `evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages gmdelta` | grounded-measurement | 326 327 > mIoU is computed per `(level, sub-task)` over the QAs that emit a `` grounding. Every sub-task 328 > grounds, so all of them get a mIoU — the only partial case is `existence_verification`, where the 329 > pure yes/no answers carry no mask and are simply excluded from its mIoU. 330 331 ## 🔁 ScanRefer & Reason3D (Tables 5–6) 332 333 Ground3D-LMM is also fine-tuned + evaluated on the ScanRefer and Reason3D referring/reasoning 334 benchmarks, in both **3D** and **3D+2D** (point cloud + the scene's 20 RGB views) settings: 335 336 | Row | Config | Checkpoint | mIoU | 337 |---|---|---|---| 338 | ScanRefer 3D | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_scanrefer.py` | `Ground3D-LMM-ScanRefer-4B-3D` | 38.72 | 339 | ScanRefer 3D+2D | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_scanrefer_image.py` | `Ground3D-LMM-ScanRefer-4B-Joint` | 41.30 | 340 | Reason3D 3D | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_reason3d.py` | `Ground3D-LMM-Reason3D-4B-3D` | 36.35 | 341 | Reason3D 3D+2D | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_reason3d_image.py` | `Ground3D-LMM-Reason3D-4B-Joint` | 41.29 | 342 343 Data prep (annotations → `*_infos.pkl` via `tools/create_data_{scanrefer,reason3d}.py`, and the 344 20-view images via `tools/build_scene_images.py`) and the eval commands are in 345 **[docs/DATA_SCANREFER_REASON3D.md](docs/DATA_SCANREFER_REASON3D.md)**. 346 347 ## 🎨 Grounding visualization 348 349 Color the model's predicted `` masks on the scene point cloud and save a `.ply` 350 (1 `` → red, 2 → red + green, N → palette). Two steps: 351 352 ```bash 353 # 1. dump predicted masks during inference (toggle on, via config or env) 354 PYTHONPATH=. python tools/test.py configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py "$CKPT" \ 355 --cfg-options model.decoder.save_viz_dir=viz_dumps ... # (or: MASK_DUMP_DIR=viz_dumps bash eval_ground3d_scannet.sh) 356 357 # 2. turn the dumps into colored point clouds (offline, no GPU/Open3D) 358 python tools/export_grounding_ply.py \ 359 --masks_dir viz_dumps --points_dir data/scannet/points --out viz_ply 360 ``` 361 362 `--mode combine` (default) writes one `.ply` per scene/conversation, coloring each grounded region 363 red, green, ...; `--mode per_qa` writes one red-masked `.ply` per question. Core writer: 364 `uniseg3d/grounding_viz.py`. For multi-turn dialogues (`task_level=multi_turn_qa_data`) each grounding 365 turn contributes one region, so a cross-object conversation produces one red object and one green 366 object in a single `.ply`. 367 368 ## 🛠️ Repository structure 369 370 ``` 371 Ground3D-LMM/ 372 ├── configs/ 373 │ ├── ground3dlmm_train.py 374 │ ├── ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py 375 │ └── ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannetpp.py 376 ├── data/ (user-populated; see Local data layout) 377 ├── docs/ 378 │ └── INSTALL.md 379 ├── tools/ 380 │ ├── train.py, test.py 381 │ ├── dist_train.sh, dist_test.sh 382 │ ├── create_data.py 383 │ └── evaluate_text_metrics.py 384 ├── uniseg3d/ (model + transforms + criteria) 385 │ ├── uniseg3d.py Grounded_LMM_main (entry point) 386 │ ├── query_decoder.py Grounded_Decoder_Joint / _Eval 387 │ ├── spconv_unet.py point encoder 388 │ ├── point_qwen3_vl.py Qwen3-VL with point-embedding injection 389 │ ├── transforms_3d.py QA_Generation_v2 / _Test 390 │ ├── unified_metric.py Part3DGlamm_SegMetric 391 │ └── ... 392 ├── work_dirs/ (checkpoints + logs, gitignored) 393 ├── train.sh one-line training launcher 394 ├── eval_ground3d_scannet.sh eval on ScanNet 395 ├── eval_ground3d_scannetpp.sh eval on ScanNet++ 396 ├── eval_ground3d_all.sh eval on both 397 ├── environment.yml conda spec (pinned versions) 398 ├── pyproject.toml 399 └── LICENSE Apache-2.0 400 ``` 401 402 ## 🙏 Acknowledgments 403 404 This codebase builds upon several open-source projects: 405 406 - **[UniSeg3D](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D)** — sparse 3D point encoder + Mask2Former-style decoder 407 - **[Qwen3-VL](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL)** — vision-language model backbone 408 - **[mmdetection3d](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d)** — 3D data pipeline and registry framework 409 - **[Mask2Former](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former)** — masked-attention decoder design 410 411 ## 📚 Citation 412 413 If you find Ground3D-LMM useful for your research, please cite: 414 415 ```bibtex 416 @inproceedings{ground3dlmm2026, 417 title = {Ground3D-LMM: Fine-Grained 3D Point Grounding 418 and Spatial Reasoning with LMM}, 419 author = {Harsh, Amol and Han, Zongyan and Lahoud, Jean 420 and Liu, Ye and Anwer, Rao Muhammad 421 and Cholakkal, Hisham and Khan, Salman 422 and Khan, Fahad Shahbaz}, 423 booktitle = {Proceedings of the European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV)}, 424 year = {2026}, 425 eprint = {2607.05493}, 426 archivePrefix = {arXiv}, 427 primaryClass = {cs.CV} 428 } 429 ``` 430 431 ## 📄 License 432 433 Released under the [Apache 2.0 License](LICENSE). 434
