# Ground3D-LMM: Fine-Grained 3D Point Grounding
and Spatial Reasoning with LMM [![arXiv](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2607.05493-b31b1b.svg?logo=arxiv&logoColor=white)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.05493) [![ECCV 2026](https://img.shields.io/badge/ECCV-2026-4b8bbe.svg)](https://amolharsh.github.io/ground3d-lmm/) [![Project Page](https://img.shields.io/badge/Project-Website-1e6cb6.svg)](https://amolharsh.github.io/ground3d-lmm/) [![Dataset](https://img.shields.io/badge/Dataset-HuggingFace-fcd734.svg?logo=huggingface&logoColor=black)](https://huggingface.co/datasets/amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache--2.0-4caf50.svg)](LICENSE) [![PyTorch](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyTorch-EE4C2C.svg?logo=pytorch&logoColor=white)](https://pytorch.org/) --- **Amol Harsh · Zongyan Han · Jean Lahoud · Ye Liu · Rao Muhammad Anwer · Hisham Cholakkal · Salman Khan · Fahad Shahbaz Khan** **Ground3D-LMM** is a large multimodal model for **fine-grained 3D point grounding** and **spatial reasoning** in indoor scenes. It produces per-point segmentation masks alongside grounded natural-language answers across **8 sub-tasks** on ScanNet and ScanNet++, trained on a **2.47M Q/A pair** dataset.
--- The architecture combines: - **SpConvUNet** sparse 3D point encoder (from UniSeg3D) - **Qwen3-VL-4B** vision-language model with LoRA fine-tuning - **Mask2Former-style query decoder** (6 layers, 256-d) - **Superpoint pooling** for efficient cross-attention over scenes ## 📢 News - **[Featured 📣]** *Ground3D-LMM* was featured by [52CV](https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/ZH2NctV9Ycg8t4EVui7gIg), a leading Chinese computer-vision community WeChat account. - **[Accepted 🎉]** *Ground3D-LMM: Fine-Grained 3D Point Grounding and Spatial Reasoning with LMM* accepted to **ECCV 2026** (main conference). - **[Released]** Code and Ground3D dataset (2.47M Q/A pairs) released on Hugging Face. ## 🏗️ Architecture ![Ground3D-LMM architecture](images/method.png) A 3D scene (XYZ + RGB point cloud) is encoded by **SpConvUNet** into per-point features, which are then pooled over precomputed superpoints to yield `Fp ∈ ℝ^(M × d)`. `Fp` is projected into two spaces in parallel: (i) into the **Qwen3-VL LMM** as `<|point|>` token embeddings alongside the text prompt and optional RGB frame, and (ii) into the **mask decoder** as keys/values for 6 layers of Mask2Former-style Cross-Attn → Self-Attn → FFN. The LMM generates text that includes `` tokens; the hidden state at each `` becomes a refined query, which is dot-producted against per-point features to produce the final segmentation mask. ## 🚀 Install ```bash conda create -n ground3d python=3.10 -y conda activate ground3d # Follow docs/INSTALL.md for the OpenMMLab stack + MinkowskiEngine (source builds), # then install this package: pip install -e . ``` > **Heads-up:** `conda env create -f environment.yml` does **not** fully work on its own — > `mmcv==2.1.0` has no prebuilt wheel for torch 2.4.1 (needs a source build with an older > `setuptools` + `--no-build-isolation`), and **MinkowskiEngine 0.5.4** must be compiled > from source. Follow [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md) **Option B** for the verified, > step-by-step install, troubleshooting, and tested environment details. **Tested**: Ubuntu 20.04 · Python 3.10 · PyTorch 2.4.1 · CUDA 11.8 · A100 80GB / RTX 3090. ## ⚡ Quick Start with HuggingFace ### Download the dataset ```python from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download # Annotations only (~3 GB) for exploration data_root = snapshot_download( repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset", repo_type="dataset", allow_patterns=["*/refined_qa_data/*", "*/part_ground3d_*.txt", "README.md"], ) # Full dataset (~150 GB) for training # data_root = snapshot_download(repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset", repo_type="dataset") ``` ### Download a pretrained checkpoint ```python from huggingface_hub import snapshot_download # Joint variant — uses 3D point cloud + aligned RGB frames (main paper result) ckpt_dir = snapshot_download(repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint") # Or the point-only variant — uses 3D points only (no RGB frames needed) # ckpt_dir = snapshot_download(repo_id="amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D") ``` ### Run inference (single config-driven invocation) Each released checkpoint has a matching eval config — the Joint (3D + 2D) variant uses `ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py` (LoRA r=16, RGB frames on), and the 3D-only variant uses `ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet_3d.py` (LoRA r=32, no RGB frames). The `_3d` config inherits from the joint one and only overrides those three fields. ```bash # --- Joint (3D + 2D) — main paper result --- CKPT="$(huggingface-cli download amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint --quiet)/pytorch_model.pth" CONFIG=configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py # --- Or, 3D-only --- # CKPT="$(huggingface-cli download amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D --quiet)/pytorch_model.pth" # CONFIG=configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet_3d.py PYTHONPATH=. python tools/test.py \ "$CONFIG" "$CKPT" \ --work-dir work_dirs/quickstart \ --cfg-options \ "model.decoder.save_pred_qa_dir=work_dirs/quickstart/preds" \ "test_dataloader.dataset.pipeline.2.transforms.2.task_level=part_qa_data" \ "test_dataloader.dataset.pipeline.2.transforms.2.task_type=qa_data" \ "test_dataloader.dataset.pipeline.2.transforms.2.sub_task=scale_estimation" ``` This runs inference for the `scale_estimation` sub-task on `part_qa_data` and writes: - Per-scene predictions to `work_dirs/quickstart/preds/{scene}.json` - Segmentation mIoU to stdout > For batched evaluation across sub-tasks or both datasets, `bash eval_ground3d.sh` auto-detects > the variant from the checkpoint's LoRA rank and picks the matching config — see the > [Evaluation](#-evaluation) section. ## 📊 Ground3D Dataset Total **2,475,307 Q/A pairs** spanning 8 sub-tasks across ScanNet and ScanNet++ scenes. | Source | Train scenes | Val scenes | Object QA | Part QA | Multi-turn | Total | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | ScanNet | 1,433 | 80 | 655,760 | 909,905 | 62,064 | 1,627,729 | | ScanNet++ | 857 | 48 | 339,396 | 498,399 | 9,783 | 847,578 | | **Total** | **2,290** | **128** | **995,156** | **1,408,304** | **71,847** | **2,475,307** | > Not every ScanNet++ scene could be used: many scenes in the ScanNet++ release are missing the depth > or mesh files our pipeline needs, and a few lost their Q/A during our VLM-based verification stage. > The scene count here may therefore differ slightly from the paper, since some scenes were listed but > held no Q/A and have been removed. **The total number of Q/A pairs is unchanged and matches the paper.** ### Sub-tasks 1. `functional_part_grounding` 2. `functional_object_grounding` 3. `scale_estimation` 4. `grounded_dimension_reasoning` 5. `relative_depth_forward` 6. `existence_verification` 7. `scale_comparison_size` 8. `distance_estimation` 9. `relative_position_forward_reasoning` Full dataset schema, Q/A JSON layout, and per-file specifications: see the [dataset card on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets/amolharsh/Ground3D_Dataset). ### Prepare the data (download → convert) **Step 1 — download** from Hugging Face. Each source (`scannet`, `scannetpp`) ships the raw per-frame arrays plus QA JSON and split lists: ``` data/scannet/ ├── processed_data//frame__vert.npy # XYZ+RGB points (load_dim=6) │ frame__sp_label.npy # superpoint ids │ frame__part_label.npy # per-point part labels │ frame__object_label.npy # per-point object labels ├── refined_qa_data/{part_qa,object_qa,multiturn_qa}//... └── part_ground3d_{train,val}.txt # scene split lists ``` **Step 2 — convert** the raw `.npy` into the flat `.bin` files and the `infos.pkl` the configs actually consume: ```bash python tools/create_data.py --dataset part3d_glamm \ --root-path data/scannet \ --out-dir data/scannet \ --qa_data_dir data/scannet/refined_qa_data ``` **ScanNet++** uses the identical layout — just swap the paths (the converter is dataset-agnostic; the ScanNet++ config reuses `data/scannet/scannet_cls_embedding.pth`): ```bash python tools/create_data.py --dataset part3d_glamm \ --root-path data/scannetpp \ --out-dir data/scannetpp \ --qa_data_dir data/scannetpp/refined_qa_data ``` Resulting layout (what the configs load via `ann_file` + `data_prefix`): ``` data/scannet/ ├── points/ super_points/ part_mask/ object_mask/ (_frame_.bin) ├── part3d_glamm_infos_train.pkl ├── part3d_glamm_infos_val.pkl └── scannet_cls_embedding.pth (shipped in this repo) ``` > **Joint model only:** the config's `model.decoder.image_dir` expects RGB frames at > `data/scannet/frame_images//.jpg`. These are ScanNet / ScanNet++ images and are > **not redistributable** (so they are not on Hugging Face). Download the raw datasets and extract > the frames each split needs by following **[docs/DATA_IMAGES.md](docs/DATA_IMAGES.md)** > (`tools/build_frame_images.py` does it straight from the `.pkl`). Or use the **3D-only** > checkpoint, which needs no images (`model.decoder.image_dir=None`). ## 🤗 Model Zoo | Model | Modality | LoRA (r / α) | Eval config | Checkpoint | |---|---|---|---|---| | Ground3D-LMM-4B (Joint) | 3D points + RGB frames | 16 / 32 | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_{scannet,scannetpp}.py` | [🤗 Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint](https://huggingface.co/amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-Joint) — main paper result | | Ground3D-LMM-4B (3D-only) | 3D points only | 32 / 64 | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_{scannet,scannetpp}_3d.py` | [🤗 Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D](https://huggingface.co/amolharsh/Ground3D-LMM-4B-3D) — no RGB frames required | Both checkpoints use **Qwen3-VL-4B** as the LLM backbone (4.47B params, ~400M LoRA-trainable). The two variants have different LoRA ranks, so each ships with its own eval config; the config inheritance keeps the diff between them tiny (`lora_r`, `lora_alpha`, `image_dir`). If you're running through `eval_ground3d.sh`, the launcher probes the checkpoint's LoRA rank and picks the matching config automatically — no manual switch needed. ## 🏋️ Training ### Prepare data 1. Download the dataset and arrange under `data/scannet/` and `data/scannetpp/` (see [Local data layout](#local-data-layout)) 2. Download pretrained sparse-conv weights into `work_dirs/pretrained/`: - `sstnet_scannet.pth` — used as the point-encoder initialization 3. The Qwen3-VL-4B base model will be downloaded automatically by `transformers`. To use a local copy, override via `--cfg-options model.decoder.qwen_model_path=/path/to/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct` ### Launch training (4 GPUs, LoRA fine-tuning) ```bash bash train.sh ``` This launches `configs/ground3dlmm_train.py` on GPUs 0-3 via `torch.distributed.launch`. Checkpoints are saved to `work_dirs/ground3dlmm/epoch_*.pth`. ### Customize the training run Common arguments to edit in `configs/ground3dlmm_train.py`: | Field | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `model.decoder.qwen_model_path` | `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct` | Path or HF id of the LLM | | `model.decoder.lora_r`, `lora_alpha` | 16, 32 | LoRA rank and scaling | | `model.decoder.max_point_tokens` | 2000 | Max superpoint tokens fed to LLM | | `train_dataloader.batch_size` | 1 | Per-GPU batch size | | `optim_wrapper.optimizer.lr` | 1e-4 | Base learning rate | | `epoch` | 10 | Total training epochs | | `load_from` | `work_dirs/pretrained/sstnet_scannet.pth` | Backbone init | ## 📈 Evaluation The paper reports **three categories of metrics**. Full evaluation is a 3-step pipeline: ### Step 1 — Run inference (segmentation mIoU + per-scene predictions) One launcher, fully argument-driven — pick the dataset / task levels / sub-tasks with flags: ```bash bash eval_ground3d.sh --checkpoint work_dirs/ground3dlmm/pytorch_model.pth # default: scannet, part+object, all sub-tasks # choose exactly what to run: bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset all --levels all # both datasets, part+object+multi_turn bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset scannet --levels part,object --sub_tasks distance_estimation,scale_estimation bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset scannetpp --levels multi_turn bash eval_ground3d.sh --help # full option list (+ --gpus, --out-root, --mask-dump) ``` `--dataset` = `scannet`|`scannetpp`|`all`; `--levels` = any of `part,object,multi_turn` (or `all`); `--sub_tasks` = `all` or a comma list. `--variant` = `joint`|`3d`|`auto` (default `auto`): the launcher inspects the checkpoint's LoRA rank (`r=16` → joint, `r=32` → 3D-only) and picks the matching config, so the Joint and 3D-only weights just work with the same command. Pass `--variant` explicitly to override. The old names `eval_ground3d_{scannet,scannetpp,all}.sh` still work — they're thin wrappers that pass flags through. Outputs: - **Segmentation mIoU** (printed per sub-task) - Per-scene prediction JSONs in `val_outputs_joint/{scannet,scannetpp}/pred_qa_data_val/...` > Add `--mask-dump ` to also dump per-QA masks (needed for the **GM-δ** stage below, and used by > the grounding visualization). `tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py` runs **two independent stages** — pick what you need via `--stages` (`ape`, `judge`, or `all`). The `--input` dir is searched **recursively**, nested / multi-turn prediction JSONs are flattened automatically, and each sample is tagged with its task. `ape` uses a text LLM (`--llm_model_path`, default `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507`) to extract numbers; `judge` uses the paper's VL judge (`--judge_model_path`, default `Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct`). Both run via **HuggingFace transformers**. Sanity-check the numeric math with `python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --selftest`. ### Step 2 — `ape` : numeric APE + δ@1.25 (the 4 numeric tasks only) ```bash python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --input val_outputs_joint/scannet/pred_qa_data_val \ --output eval_results/scannet_ape.json --stages ape \ --llm_model_path Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 --gpus 0,1,2,3 ``` Runs **only** on `distance_estimation`, `grounded_dimension_reasoning`, `scale_estimation`, `scale_comparison_size`. The LLM extracts the scalar(s) in metres (per-task JSON shape; a missing prediction → `0.0` so it is penalised), then reports **APE** `|ŝ−s|/s×100%` and **δ@1.25** success (`δ = max(ŝ/s, s/ŝ) ≤ 1.25`; GT==0 pairs skipped; mean over pairs, then macro-averaged per task). ### Step 3 — `judge` : LLM judge — Hallucination + Completeness (all tasks) ```bash python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --input val_outputs_joint/scannet/pred_qa_data_val \ --output eval_results/scannet_judge.json --stages judge \ --judge_model_path Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct --gpus 0,1,2,3 ``` The Table-4 judge — **Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct** — scores each prediction and reports **Hallucination** and **Completeness** (over all tasks). Run both stages with `--stages all` (the `ape` extractor stays on the text `Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507`). ### Step 3b — `gmdelta` : GM-δ (supplementary, opt-in) GM-δ (Grounded-Measurement) counts a prediction correct only when **mask IoU > 0.3 AND δ ≤ 1.25**, on the numeric tasks that also ground. Run the numeric sub-tasks **with `--mask-dump`** (the mask tree mirrors the prediction tree), then **one command auto-iterates all 4 numeric tasks × both datasets**: ```bash # 1. inference for the 4 numeric tasks on both datasets, dumping per-QA masks bash eval_ground3d.sh --dataset all --levels part \ --sub_tasks distance_estimation,grounded_dimension_reasoning,scale_estimation,scale_comparison_size \ --mask-dump masks --checkpoint work_dirs/ground3dlmm/pytorch_model.pth # 2. GM-δ across all of them in a single run python tools/evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages gmdelta \ --input val_outputs_joint --mask_dump_dir masks \ --llm_model_path Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 --gpus 0,1,2,3 --output eval_results/gmdelta.json ``` It reports GM-δ **per (dataset, task)** and **overall**. `--gmdelta_task all` (default) auto-discovers the numeric tasks; pass a single task name to restrict. ### Metric provenance (the paper's metrics) | Metric | Provided by | Tasks | |---|---|---| | Segmentation mIoU | `tools/test.py` → `Part3DGlamm_SegMetric` | all sub-tasks (over each QA's `` grounding) | | APE & δ@1.25 (LLM-extracted) | `evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages ape` | 4 numeric tasks | | Hallucination + Completeness (LLM judge) | `evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages judge` | all tasks | | GM-δ (IoU>0.3 ∧ δ≤1.25), *supplementary* | `evaluate_text_metrics.py --stages gmdelta` | grounded-measurement | > mIoU is computed per `(level, sub-task)` over the QAs that emit a `` grounding. Every sub-task > grounds, so all of them get a mIoU — the only partial case is `existence_verification`, where the > pure yes/no answers carry no mask and are simply excluded from its mIoU. ## 🔁 ScanRefer & Reason3D (Tables 5–6) Ground3D-LMM is also fine-tuned + evaluated on the ScanRefer and Reason3D referring/reasoning benchmarks, in both **3D** and **3D+2D** (point cloud + the scene's 20 RGB views) settings: | Row | Config | Checkpoint | mIoU | |---|---|---|---| | ScanRefer 3D | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_scanrefer.py` | `Ground3D-LMM-ScanRefer-4B-3D` | 38.72 | | ScanRefer 3D+2D | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_scanrefer_image.py` | `Ground3D-LMM-ScanRefer-4B-Joint` | 41.30 | | Reason3D 3D | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_reason3d.py` | `Ground3D-LMM-Reason3D-4B-3D` | 36.35 | | Reason3D 3D+2D | `configs/ground3dlmm_eval_reason3d_image.py` | `Ground3D-LMM-Reason3D-4B-Joint` | 41.29 | Data prep (annotations → `*_infos.pkl` via `tools/create_data_{scanrefer,reason3d}.py`, and the 20-view images via `tools/build_scene_images.py`) and the eval commands are in **[docs/DATA_SCANREFER_REASON3D.md](docs/DATA_SCANREFER_REASON3D.md)**. ## 🎨 Grounding visualization Color the model's predicted `` masks on the scene point cloud and save a `.ply` (1 `` → red, 2 → red + green, N → palette). Two steps: ```bash # 1. dump predicted masks during inference (toggle on, via config or env) PYTHONPATH=. python tools/test.py configs/ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py "$CKPT" \ --cfg-options model.decoder.save_viz_dir=viz_dumps ... # (or: MASK_DUMP_DIR=viz_dumps bash eval_ground3d_scannet.sh) # 2. turn the dumps into colored point clouds (offline, no GPU/Open3D) python tools/export_grounding_ply.py \ --masks_dir viz_dumps --points_dir data/scannet/points --out viz_ply ``` `--mode combine` (default) writes one `.ply` per scene/conversation, coloring each grounded region red, green, ...; `--mode per_qa` writes one red-masked `.ply` per question. Core writer: `uniseg3d/grounding_viz.py`. For multi-turn dialogues (`task_level=multi_turn_qa_data`) each grounding turn contributes one region, so a cross-object conversation produces one red object and one green object in a single `.ply`. ## 🛠️ Repository structure ``` Ground3D-LMM/ ├── configs/ │ ├── ground3dlmm_train.py │ ├── ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannet.py │ └── ground3dlmm_eval_ground3d_scannetpp.py ├── data/ (user-populated; see Local data layout) ├── docs/ │ └── INSTALL.md ├── tools/ │ ├── train.py, test.py │ ├── dist_train.sh, dist_test.sh │ ├── create_data.py │ └── evaluate_text_metrics.py ├── uniseg3d/ (model + transforms + criteria) │ ├── uniseg3d.py Grounded_LMM_main (entry point) │ ├── query_decoder.py Grounded_Decoder_Joint / _Eval │ ├── spconv_unet.py point encoder │ ├── point_qwen3_vl.py Qwen3-VL with point-embedding injection │ ├── transforms_3d.py QA_Generation_v2 / _Test │ ├── unified_metric.py Part3DGlamm_SegMetric │ └── ... ├── work_dirs/ (checkpoints + logs, gitignored) ├── train.sh one-line training launcher ├── eval_ground3d_scannet.sh eval on ScanNet ├── eval_ground3d_scannetpp.sh eval on ScanNet++ ├── eval_ground3d_all.sh eval on both ├── environment.yml conda spec (pinned versions) ├── pyproject.toml └── LICENSE Apache-2.0 ``` ## 🙏 Acknowledgments This codebase builds upon several open-source projects: - **[UniSeg3D](https://github.com/dk-liang/UniSeg3D)** — sparse 3D point encoder + Mask2Former-style decoder - **[Qwen3-VL](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen3-VL)** — vision-language model backbone - **[mmdetection3d](https://github.com/open-mmlab/mmdetection3d)** — 3D data pipeline and registry framework - **[Mask2Former](https://github.com/facebookresearch/Mask2Former)** — masked-attention decoder design ## 📚 Citation If you find Ground3D-LMM useful for your research, please cite: ```bibtex @inproceedings{ground3dlmm2026, title = {Ground3D-LMM: Fine-Grained 3D Point Grounding and Spatial Reasoning with LMM}, author = {Harsh, Amol and Han, Zongyan and Lahoud, Jean and Liu, Ye and Anwer, Rao Muhammad and Cholakkal, Hisham and Khan, Salman and Khan, Fahad Shahbaz}, booktitle = {Proceedings of the European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV)}, year = {2026}, eprint = {2607.05493}, archivePrefix = {arXiv}, primaryClass = {cs.CV} } ``` ## 📄 License Released under the [Apache 2.0 License](LICENSE).

33	def preprocess_chatml(input_ids, text, tokenizer, qwen_model='qwen3_vl'):
34	    """Build training labels from a ChatML conversation.
35	
36	    Loss is computed **only on the assistant replies**: every other span
37	    (system prompt, user turns, role headers) is masked with ``IGNORE_INDEX``,
38	    as is the trailing incomplete assistant turn (the generation prompt).
39	
40	    Args:
41	        input_ids (torch.Tensor): ``(1, L)`` token ids of the full conversation.
42	        text (str): the same conversation as a string (used to split rounds).
43	        tokenizer: the LMM tokenizer (``self.processor.tokenizer``).
44	        qwen_model (str): ``'qwen2_5_vl'`` or ``'qwen3_vl'`` — selects the
45	            ChatML system prompt via :func:`~uniseg3d.conversation.get_conv`.
46	
47	    Returns:
48	        torch.Tensor: labels shaped like ``input_ids``, masked with ``IGNORE_INDEX``.
49	    """
50	    conv = get_conv('chatml', qwen_model=qwen_model)
51	    rounds = [m + conv.seps[0] for m in text.split(conv.seps[0])]
52	
53	    # the final chunk is the incomplete assistant turn -> never supervised
54	    last_invalide_text = rounds[-1]
55	    rounds = rounds[:-1]
56	
57	    if conv.system is None:
58	        rounds = [''.join(rounds[i:i + 2]) for i in range(0, len(rounds), 2)]
59	    else:
60	        rounds = [''.join(rounds[:3])] + [''.join(rounds[i:i + 2]) for i in range(3, len(rounds), 2)]
61	
62	    labels = input_ids.clone()
63	
64	    sep = conv.seps[0] + conv.roles[1]
65	    cur_len = 0
66	
67	    for rou in rounds:
68	        if len(rou) == 0:
69	            break
70	
71	        # mask everything up to and including the assistant header
72	        ins = sep.join(rou.split(sep)[:-1]) + sep
73	        rou_len = tokenizer(rou, return_length=True).length[0]
74	        ins_len = tokenizer(ins, return_length=True).length[0]
75	        labels[:, cur_len:cur_len + ins_len] = IGNORE_INDEX
76	        cur_len += rou_len
77	
78	    if (labels == IGNORE_INDEX).sum() == labels.size(1):
79	        raise ValueError('No valid labels found')
80	
81	    last_invalide = tokenizer(last_invalide_text, return_length=True).length[0]
82	    labels[:, -last_invalide + 1:] = IGNORE_INDEX
83	
84	    return labels

87	class ConvSetAggregator(nn.Module):
88	    """Aggregate variable-length point features into a fixed number of tokens
89	    using 1D convolution across the set dimension followed by adaptive pooling.
90	
91	    Args:
92	        in_channels (int): Feature dimension per point.
93	        out_tokens (int): Number of aggregated tokens.
94	        kernel_size (int): Convolution kernel size for the first layer.
95	        hidden_channels (int | None): Hidden channels; defaults to in_channels.
96	    """
97	    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_tokens, kernel_size=5, hidden_channels=None):
98	        super().__init__()
99	        hidden = in_channels if hidden_channels is None else hidden_channels
100	        padding = kernel_size // 2
101	        self.net = nn.Sequential(
102	            nn.Conv1d(in_channels, hidden, kernel_size=kernel_size, padding=padding),
103	            nn.GELU(),
104	            nn.Conv1d(hidden, in_channels, kernel_size=3, padding=1),
105	            nn.GELU(),
106	        )
107	        self.pool = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool1d(out_tokens)
108	
109	    def forward(self, x):
110	        # x: (N, D)
111	        if x.dim() != 2:
112	            raise ValueError('ConvSetAggregator expects 2D tensor of shape (N, D)')
113	        n, d = x.shape
114	        x1 = x.transpose(0, 1).unsqueeze(0)  # (1, D, N)
115	        y = self.net(x1)
116	        y = self.pool(y)  # (1, D, K)
117	        y = y.squeeze(0).transpose(0, 1)  # (K, D)
118	        return y

120	class PositionSoftClusterAggregator(nn.Module):
121	    """Position-aware soft clustering aggregator.
122	
123	    Aggregates features into K tokens using soft assignment based on
124	    Euclidean distance between normalized point positions and learnable
125	    prototype centers. Permutation-invariant and driven by spatial layout.
126	
127	    Args:
128	        in_channels (int): Feature dimension per point.
129	        out_tokens (int): Number of aggregated tokens (cluster centers).
130	        pos_dim (int): Dimensionality of positions (default 3).
131	        temperature (float): Softmax temperature over negative distances.
132	    """
133	    def __init__(self, in_channels, out_tokens, pos_dim=3, temperature=0.5):
134	        super().__init__()
135	        self.out_tokens = out_tokens
136	        self.temperature = temperature
137	        self.register_parameter(
138	            'centers', nn.Parameter(torch.randn(out_tokens, pos_dim)))
139	
140	    def forward(self, feats, pos):
141	        # feats: (N, D), pos: (N, P)
142	        if feats.dim() != 2 or pos.dim() != 2:
143	            raise ValueError('PositionSoftClusterAggregator expects 2D tensors (N, D) and (N, P)')
144	        if feats.shape[0] != pos.shape[0]:
145	            raise ValueError('feats and pos must have same first dimension N')
146	        # normalize positions per-sample
147	        p = pos.float()
148	        p = p - p.mean(dim=0, keepdim=True)
149	        std = p.std(dim=0, keepdim=True) + 1e-6
150	        p = p / std
151	        # distances to centers: (N, K)
152	        diff = p.unsqueeze(1) - self.centers.unsqueeze(0)
153	        dist = (diff ** 2).sum(-1)
154	        assign = torch.softmax(-dist / max(self.temperature, 1e-6), dim=1)  # (N, K)
155	        # aggregate features: (K, D)
156	        num = assign.sum(dim=0, keepdim=True).transpose(0, 1) + 1e-6  # (K, 1)
157	        agg = assign.transpose(0, 1) @ feats  # (K, D)
158	        agg = agg / num
159	        return agg

162	class FPSAggregator(nn.Module):
163	    """Farthest Point Sampling (FPS) aggregator.
164	    
165	    Samples a fixed number of points using FPS algorithm based on feature distances.

175	    def forward(self, x):
176	        # x: (N, D)
177	        if x.dim() != 2:
178	            raise ValueError('FPSAggregator expects 2D tensor of shape (N, D)')
179	        n, d = x.shape
180	        
181	        if n <= self.out_tokens:
182	            return x
183	        
184	        # FPS sampling based on feature L2 distances
185	        indices = self.fps_sample(x, self.out_tokens)

189	    def fps_sample(points, num_samples):
190	        """Farthest Point Sampling.
191	        
192	        Args:
193	            points: (N, D) tensor
194	            num_samples: number of samples to select
195	            
196	        Returns:
197	            indices: (num_samples,) tensor of selected indices
198	        """
199	        n = points.shape[0]
200	        device = points.device
201	        
202	        # Start with a random point
203	        indices = torch.zeros(num_samples, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
204	        distances = torch.ones(n, device=device) * float('inf')
205	        
206	        # Compute pairwise distances
207	        dist_matrix = torch.cdist(points, points)  # (N, N)
208	        
209	        # First point: random
210	        current = torch.randint(0, n, (1,), device=device).item()
211	        indices[0] = current
212	        
213	        for i in range(1, num_samples):
214	            # Update distances to the current farthest point
215	            dist_to_current = dist_matrix[current]  # (N,)
216	            distances = torch.minimum(distances, dist_to_current)
217	            
218	            # Select the farthest point
219	            current = distances.argmax().item()
220	            indices[i] = current
221	        
222	        return indices

292	def mask_pool(x, mask):
293	    """
294	    Args:
295	        x: [D, M]
296	        mask: [N, M]
297	    """
298	    with torch.no_grad():
299	        mask = mask.detach()
300	        mask = (mask > 0).to(mask.dtype)
301	        denorm = mask.sum(dim=(-1), keepdim=True) + 1e-8
302	
303	    mask_pooled_x = torch.einsum(
304	        "dm,nm->nd",
305	        x,
306	        mask / denorm,
307	    )
308	    return mask_pooled_x

322	        self.fix = fix
323	        self.attn = nn.MultiheadAttention(
324	            d_model, num_heads, dropout=dropout, batch_first=True)
325	        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
326	        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
327	        # todo: why BaseModule doesn't call it without us?
328	        self.init_weights()

330	    def init_weights(self):
331	        """Init weights."""
332	        for p in self.parameters():
333	            if p.dim() > 1:
334	                nn.init.xavier_uniform_(p)
335	
336	    def forward(self, sources, queries, attn_masks=None):
337	        """Forward pass.
338	
339	        Args:
340	            sources (List[Tensor]): of len batch_size,
341	                each of shape (n_points_i, d_model).
342	            queries (List[Tensor]): of len batch_size,
343	                each of shape(n_queries_i, d_model).
344	            attn_masks (List[Tensor] or None): of len batch_size,
345	                each of shape (n_queries, n_points).
346	        
347	        Return:
348	            List[Tensor]: Queries of len batch_size,
349	                each of shape(n_queries_i, d_model).
350	        """
351	        outputs = []
352	        for i in range(len(sources)):
353	            k = v = sources[i]
354	            attn_mask = attn_masks[i] if attn_masks is not None else None
355	            output, _ = self.attn(queries[i], k, v, attn_mask=attn_mask)
356	            if self.fix:
357	                output = self.dropout(output)
358	            output = output + queries[i]
359	            if self.fix:
360	                output = self.norm(output)
361	            outputs.append(output)
362	        return outputs

365	class SelfAttentionLayer(BaseModule):
366	    """Self attention layer.
367	
368	    Args:
369	        d_model (int): Model dimension.
370	        num_heads (int): Number of heads.
371	        dropout (float): Dropout rate.
372	    """
373	
374	    def __init__(self, d_model, num_heads, dropout):
375	        super().__init__()
376	        self.attn = nn.MultiheadAttention(
377	            d_model, num_heads, dropout=dropout, batch_first=True)
378	        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
379	        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
380	
381	    def forward(self, x, interaction_masks=None):
382	        """Forward pass.
383	
384	        Args:
385	            x (List[Tensor]): Queries of len batch_size,
386	                each of shape(n_queries_i, d_model).
387	        
388	        Returns:
389	            List[Tensor]: Queries of len batch_size,
390	                each of shape(n_queries_i, d_model).
391	        """
392	        out = []
393	
394	
395	        
396	
397	        for i, y in enumerate(x):
398	            nan_mask = torch.isnan(y).any(dim=-1)  # shape: (num_queries,)
399	        
400	            # replace NaN with 0
401	            y_safe = y.clone()
402	            y_safe[nan_mask] = 0.0
403	            if not interaction_masks:
404	                z, _ = self.attn(y_safe, y_safe, y_safe)
405	            else:
406	                z, _ = self.attn(y_safe, y_safe, y_safe, attn_mask=interaction_masks[i])
407	            z = self.dropout(z) + y
408	            z = self.norm(z)
409	            out.append(z)
410	        return out

413	class FFN(BaseModule):
414	    """Feed forward network.
415	
416	    Args:
417	        d_model (int): Model dimension.
418	        hidden_dim (int): Hidden dimension.
419	        dropout (float): Dropout rate.
420	        activation_fn (str): 'relu' or 'gelu'.

422	
423	    def __init__(self, d_model, hidden_dim, dropout, activation_fn):
424	        super().__init__()
425	        self.net = nn.Sequential(
426	            nn.Linear(d_model, hidden_dim),
427	            nn.ReLU() if activation_fn == 'relu' else nn.GELU(),
428	            nn.Dropout(dropout),
429	            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, d_model),
430	            nn.Dropout(dropout))
431	        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
432	
433	    def forward(self, x):
434	        """Forward pass.
435	
436	        Args:
437	            x (List[Tensor]): Queries of len batch_size,
438	                each of shape(n_queries_i, d_model).
439	        
440	        Returns:
441	            List[Tensor]: Queries of len batch_size,
442	                each of shape(n_queries_i, d_model).
443	        """
444	        out = []
445	        for y in x:
446	            z = self.net(y)

448	            z = self.norm(z)

453	class QueryDecoder(BaseModule):
454	    """Query decoder.
455	
456	    Args:
457	        num_layers (int): Number of transformer layers.
458	        num_instance_queries (int): Number of instance queries.
459	        num_semantic_queries (int): Number of semantic queries.
460	        num_classes (int): Number of classes.
461	        in_channels (int): Number of input channels.
462	        d_model (int): Number of channels for model layers.
463	        num_heads (int): Number of head in attention layer.
464	        hidden_dim (int): Dimension of attention layer.
465	        dropout (float): Dropout rate for transformer layer.
466	        activation_fn (str): 'relu' of 'gelu'.
467	        iter_pred (bool): Whether to predict iteratively.
468	        attn_mask (bool): Whether to use mask attention.
469	        pos_enc_flag (bool): Whether to use positional enconding.
470	    """
471	
472	    def __init__(self, num_layers, num_instance_queries, num_semantic_queries,
473	                 num_classes, in_channels, d_model, num_heads, hidden_dim,
474	                 dropout, activation_fn, iter_pred, attn_mask, fix_attention,
475	                 objectness_flag, sphere_cls, **kwargs):
476	        super().__init__()
477	        self.objectness_flag = objectness_flag
478	        self.sphere_cls = sphere_cls
479	        self.input_proj = nn.Sequential(
480	            nn.Linear(in_channels, d_model), nn.LayerNorm(d_model), nn.ReLU())
481	        self.num_queries = num_instance_queries + num_semantic_queries
482	        if num_instance_queries + num_semantic_queries > 0:
483	            self.query = nn.Embedding(num_instance_queries + num_semantic_queries, d_model)
484	        if num_instance_queries == 0:
485	            self.query_proj = nn.Sequential(
486	                nn.Linear(in_channels, d_model), nn.ReLU(),
487	                nn.Linear(d_model, d_model))
488	        self.cross_attn_layers = nn.ModuleList([])
489	        self.self_attn_layers = nn.ModuleList([])
490	        self.ffn_layers = nn.ModuleList([])
491	        for i in range(num_layers):
492	            self.cross_attn_layers.append(
493	                CrossAttentionLayer(
494	                    d_model, num_heads, dropout, fix_attention))
495	            self.self_attn_layers.append(
496	                SelfAttentionLayer(d_model, num_heads, dropout))
497	            self.ffn_layers.append(
498	                FFN(d_model, hidden_dim, dropout, activation_fn))
499	        self.out_norm = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
500	        if not self.sphere_cls:
501	            self.out_cls = nn.Sequential(
502	                nn.Linear(d_model, d_model), nn.ReLU(),
503	                nn.Linear(d_model, num_classes + 1))
504	        if objectness_flag:
505	            self.out_score = nn.Sequential(
506	                nn.Linear(d_model, d_model), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(d_model, 1))
507	        self.x_mask = nn.Sequential(
508	            nn.Linear(in_channels, d_model), nn.ReLU(),
509	            nn.Linear(d_model, d_model))
510	        self.iter_pred = iter_pred
511	        self.attn_mask = attn_mask
512	    
513	    def _get_queries(self, queries=None, batch_size=None):
514	        """Get query tensor.
515	
516	        Args:
517	            queries (List[Tensor], optional): of len batch_size,
518	                each of shape (n_queries_i, in_channels).
519	            batch_size (int, optional): batch size.
520	        
521	        Returns:
522	            List[Tensor]: of len batch_size, each of shape
523	                (n_queries_i, d_model).
524	        """
525	        if batch_size is None:
526	            batch_size = len(queries)
527	        
528	        result_queries = []
529	        for i in range(batch_size):
530	            result_query = []
531	            if hasattr(self, 'query'):
532	                result_query.append(self.query.weight)
533	            if queries is not None:
534	                result_query.append(self.query_proj(queries[i]))
535	            result_queries.append(torch.cat(result_query))
536	        return result_queries
537	
538	    def _forward_head(self, queries, mask_feats):
539	        """Prediction head forward.
540	
541	        Args:
542	            queries (List[Tensor] | Tensor): List of len batch_size,
543	                each of shape (n_queries_i, d_model). Or tensor of
544	                shape (batch_size, n_queries, d_model).
545	            mask_feats (List[Tensor]): of len batch_size,
546	                each of shape (n_points_i, d_model).
547	
548	        Returns:
549	            Tuple:
550	                List[Tensor]: Classification predictions of len batch_size,
551	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_classes + 1).
552	                List[Tensor]: Confidence scores of len batch_size,
553	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, 1).
554	                List[Tensor]: Predicted masks of len batch_size,
555	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_points_i).
556	                List[Tensor] or None: Attention masks of len batch_size,
557	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_points_i).
558	        """
559	        cls_preds, pred_scores, pred_masks, attn_masks = [], [], [], []
560	        for i in range(len(queries)):
561	            norm_query = self.out_norm(queries[i])
562	            cls_preds.append(self.out_cls(norm_query))
563	            pred_score = self.out_score(norm_query) if self.objectness_flag \
564	                else None
565	            pred_scores.append(pred_score)
566	            pred_mask = torch.einsum('nd,md->nm', norm_query, mask_feats[i])
567	            if self.attn_mask:
568	                attn_mask = (pred_mask.sigmoid() < 0.5).bool()
569	                attn_mask[torch.where(
570	                    attn_mask.sum(-1) == attn_mask.shape[-1])] = False
571	                attn_mask = attn_mask.detach()
572	                attn_masks.append(attn_mask)
573	            pred_masks.append(pred_mask)
574	        attn_masks = attn_masks if self.attn_mask else None
575	        return cls_preds, pred_scores, pred_masks, attn_masks
576	
577	    def forward_simple(self, x, queries):
578	        """Simple forward pass.
579	        
580	        Args:
581	            x (List[Tensor]): of len batch_size, each of shape
582	                (n_points_i, in_channels).
583	            queries (List[Tensor], optional): of len batch_size, each of shape
584	                (n_points_i, in_channles).
585	        
586	        Returns:
587	            Dict: with labels, masks, and scores.
588	        """
589	        inst_feats = [self.input_proj(y) for y in x]
590	        mask_feats = [self.x_mask(y) for y in x]
591	        queries = self._get_queries(queries, len(x))
592	        for i in range(len(self.cross_attn_layers)):
593	            queries = self.cross_attn_layers[i](inst_feats, queries)
594	            queries = self.self_attn_layers[i](queries)
595	            queries = self.ffn_layers[i](queries)
596	        cls_preds, pred_scores, pred_masks, _ = self._forward_head(
597	            queries, mask_feats)
598	        return dict(
599	            cls_preds=cls_preds,
600	            masks=pred_masks,
601	            scores=pred_scores)
602	
603	    def forward_iter_pred(self, x, queries):
604	        """Iterative forward pass.
605	        
606	        Args:
607	            x (List[Tensor]): of len batch_size, each of shape
608	                (n_points_i, in_channels).
609	            queries (List[Tensor], optional): of len batch_size, each of shape
610	                (n_points_i, in_channles).
611	        
612	        Returns:
613	            Dict: with labels, masks, scores, and aux_outputs.
614	        """
615	        cls_preds, pred_scores, pred_masks = [], [], []
616	        inst_feats = [self.input_proj(y) for y in x]
617	        mask_feats = [self.x_mask(y) for y in x]
618	        queries = self._get_queries(queries, len(x))
619	        cls_pred, pred_score, pred_mask, attn_mask = self._forward_head(
620	            queries, mask_feats)
621	        cls_preds.append(cls_pred)
622	        pred_scores.append(pred_score)
623	        pred_masks.append(pred_mask)
624	        for i in range(len(self.cross_attn_layers)):
625	            queries = self.cross_attn_layers[i](inst_feats, queries, attn_mask)
626	            queries = self.self_attn_layers[i](queries)
627	            queries = self.ffn_layers[i](queries)
628	            cls_pred, pred_score, pred_mask, attn_mask = self._forward_head(
629	                queries, mask_feats)
630	            cls_preds.append(cls_pred)
631	            pred_scores.append(pred_score)
632	            pred_masks.append(pred_mask)
633	
634	        aux_outputs = [
635	            {'cls_preds': cls_pred, 'masks': masks, 'scores': scores}
636	            for cls_pred, scores, masks in zip(
637	                cls_preds[:-1], pred_scores[:-1], pred_masks[:-1])]
638	        return dict(
639	            cls_preds=cls_preds[-1],
640	            masks=pred_masks[-1],
641	            scores=pred_scores[-1],
642	            aux_outputs=aux_outputs)
643	
644	    def forward(self, x, queries=None, interaction_masks=None):
645	        """Forward pass.
646	        
647	        Args:
648	            x (List[Tensor]): of len batch_size, each of shape
649	                (n_points_i, in_channels).
650	            queries (List[Tensor], optional): of len batch_size, each of shape
651	                (n_points_i, in_channles).
652	        
653	        Returns:
654	            Dict: with labels, masks, scores, and possibly aux_outputs.
655	        """
656	        if self.iter_pred:
657	            return self.forward_iter_pred(x, queries, interaction_masks=interaction_masks)
658	        else:
659	            return self.forward_simple(x, queries)

666	    def __init__(self, num_instance_classes, num_semantic_classes,

670	        if not self.sphere_cls:

674	                    nn.Linear(d_model, d_model), nn.ReLU(),
675	                    nn.Linear(d_model, num_semantic_classes + 1))
676	            else:
677	                self.out_sem = nn.Linear(d_model, num_semantic_classes + 1)
678	            
679	        if self.sphere_cls:
680	            rank, world_size = get_dist_info()
681	            cls_embed = torch.load(vocabulary_cls_embedding_path)
682	            
683	            _dim = cls_embed.size(2)
684	            _prototypes = cls_embed.size(1)
685	
686	            if rank == 0:
687	                back_token = torch.zeros(1, _dim, dtype=torch.float32, device='cuda')
688	            else:
689	                back_token = torch.empty(1, _dim, dtype=torch.float32, device='cuda')
690	            if world_size > 1:
691	                dist.broadcast(back_token, src=0)
692	            back_token = back_token.to(device='cpu')
693	            cls_embed = torch.cat([
694	                cls_embed, back_token.repeat(_prototypes, 1)[None]
695	            ], dim=0)
696	            self.register_buffer('cls_embed', cls_embed.permute(2, 0, 1).contiguous(), persistent=False)
697	            
698	            cls_embed_dim = self.cls_embed.size(0)
699	            self.cls_proj = nn.Sequential(
700	                nn.Linear(d_model, d_model), nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
701	                nn.Linear(d_model, d_model), nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
702	                nn.Linear(d_model, cls_embed_dim))
703	            
704	            self.cls_proj_sem = nn.Sequential(
705	                nn.Linear(d_model, d_model), nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
706	                nn.Linear(d_model, d_model), nn.ReLU(inplace=True),
707	                nn.Linear(d_model, cls_embed_dim))
708	            
709	            logit_scale = torch.tensor(4.6052, dtype=torch.float32)
710	            self.register_buffer('logit_scale', logit_scale, persistent=False)
711	            
712	            # Mask Pooling
713	            self.mask_pooling = mask_pool
714	            self.mask_pooling_proj = nn.Sequential(
715	                nn.LayerNorm(d_model),
716	                nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
717	            )
718	            
719	            self.mask_pooling_proj_sem = nn.Sequential(
720	                nn.LayerNorm(d_model),
721	                nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
722	            )
723	    def forward_logit(self, cls_embd, sem=False):
724	        if sem:
725	            cls_pred = torch.einsum('nd,dkp->nkp', F.normalize(cls_embd, dim=-1), self.cls_embed)
726	        else:
727	            cls_pred = torch.einsum('nd,dkp->nkp', F.normalize(cls_embd, dim=-1), self.cls_embed[:, 2:, :])
728	        cls_pred = cls_pred.max(-1).values
729	        cls_pred = self.logit_scale.exp() * cls_pred
730	        return cls_pred

732	    def _forward_head(self, queries, mask_feats, last_flag):
733	        """Prediction head forward.
734	
735	        Args:
736	            queries (List[Tensor] | Tensor): List of len batch_size,
737	                each of shape (n_queries_i, d_model). Or tensor of
738	                shape (batch_size, n_queries, d_model).

744	                List[Tensor]: Classification predictions of len batch_size,
745	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_instance_classes + 1).

747	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_semantic_classes + 1).
748	                List[Tensor]: Confidence scores of len batch_size,
749	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, 1).
750	                List[Tensor]: Predicted masks of len batch_size,

752	                List[Tensor] or None: Attention masks of len batch_size,
753	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_points_i).
754	        """
755	        cls_preds, sem_preds, pred_scores, pred_masks, attn_masks = \
756	            [], [], [], [], []
757	        for i in range(len(queries)):
758	            norm_query = self.out_norm(queries[i])
759	            if not self.sphere_cls:

764	            pred_score = self.out_score(norm_query) if self.objectness_flag \

769	            if self.sphere_cls:

774	                cls_pred = self.forward_logit(cls_embd) 
775	                cls_preds.append(cls_pred)
776	                if last_flag:
777	                    norm_query_sem = norm_query.clone()
778	                    maskpool_embd_sem  = self.mask_pooling_proj_sem(maskpool_)
779	                    cls_embd_sem = self.cls_proj_sem(maskpool_embd_sem + norm_query_sem)
780	                    cls_pred_sem = self.forward_logit(cls_embd_sem, sem=True)
781	                    sem_preds.append(cls_pred_sem)
782	                
783	            if self.attn_mask:
784	                attn_mask = (pred_mask.sigmoid() < 0.5).bool()
785	                attn_mask[torch.where(
786	                    attn_mask.sum(-1) == attn_mask.shape[-1])] = False
787	                attn_mask = attn_mask.detach()
788	                attn_masks.append(attn_mask)

790	        attn_masks = attn_masks if self.attn_mask else None
791	        sem_preds = sem_preds if last_flag else None
792	        return cls_preds, sem_preds, pred_scores, pred_masks, attn_masks

843	        pred_masks.append(pred_mask)
844	        contras_embeds.append([self.out_norm(queries[i].clone()) for i in range(len(queries))])
845	        
846	        for i in range(len(self.cross_attn_layers)):

848	            queries = self.self_attn_layers[i](queries, interaction_masks=interaction_masks)

1050	    def get_query_tokens(self, hidden_states, input_ids, text, num_qa):
1051	        """
1052	        Extract query tokens from hidden_states, grouped by QA pair.
1053	
1054	        Following preprocess_chatml's rounds splitting, determine the token range of each
1055	        assistant reply, then extract embeddings between <p>...</p> within that range.
1056	
1057	        Args:
1058	            hidden_states: hidden states of the model's last layer, shape (1, seq_len, hidden_dim)
1059	            input_ids: input token ids, shape (1, seq_len)
1060	            text: full text after apply_chat_template
1061	            num_qa: number of QA pairs
1062	
1063	        Returns:
1064	            list of query tokens, length num_qa, each element is a (num_queries, hidden_dim) tensor
1065	        """
1066	        hidden_dim = hidden_states.shape[-1]
1067	        device = hidden_states.device
1068	        tokenizer = self.processor.tokenizer
1069	
1070	        # get ids of special tokens
1071	        p_start_id = self.seg_tokens_ids[0]  # <p>
1072	        p_end_id = self.seg_tokens_ids[1]    # </p>
1073	
1074	        input_ids_flat = input_ids[0]  # (seq_len,)
1075	        hidden_flat = hidden_states[0]  # (seq_len, hidden_dim)
1076	
1077	        # find positions of all <p> and </p>
1078	        p_start_positions = (input_ids_flat == p_start_id).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0].tolist()
1079	        p_end_positions = (input_ids_flat == p_end_id).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0].tolist()
1080	
1081	        # follow preprocess_chatml splitting
1082	        conv = get_conv('chatml', qwen_model=self.base_model)
1083	        rounds = [m + conv.seps[0] for m in text.split(conv.seps[0])]
1084	        rounds = rounds[:-1]  # drop the final empty round
1085	
1086	        # grouping: system + user + assistant as one group, then every two (user + assistant) as a group
1087	        if conv.system is None:
1088	            grouped_rounds = [''.join(rounds[i:i + 2]) for i in range(0, len(rounds), 2)]
1089	        else:
1090	            grouped_rounds = [''.join(rounds[:3])] + [''.join(rounds[i:i + 2]) for i in range(3, len(rounds), 2)]
1091	
1092	        # separator: used to split instruction and assistant reply
1093	        sep = conv.seps[0] + conv.roles[1]  # '<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n'
1094	
1095	        all_query_tokens = []
1096	        cur_len = 0
1097	
1098	        for i, rou in enumerate(grouped_rounds):
1099	            if i >= num_qa:
1100	                break
1101	            if len(rou) == 0:
1102	                all_query_tokens.append(torch.zeros(1, hidden_dim, device=device))
1103	                continue
1104	
1105	            # compute the token length of this round
1106	            rou_len = tokenizer(rou, return_length=True).length[0]
1107	
1108	            # split instruction and assistant reply
1109	            parts = rou.split(sep)
1110	            if len(parts) < 2:
1111	                # no assistant reply
1112	                all_query_tokens.append(torch.zeros(1, hidden_dim, device=device))
1113	                cur_len += rou_len
1114	                continue
1115	
1116	            ins = sep.join(parts[:-1]) + sep
1117	            ins_len = tokenizer(ins, return_length=True).length[0]
1118	
1119	            # token range of assistant reply
1120	            assistant_start = cur_len + ins_len
1121	            assistant_end = cur_len + rou_len
1122	
1123	            # find <p>...</p> within this range
1124	            qa_queries = []
1125	            used_end_positions = set()
1126	
1127	            for p_start in p_start_positions:
1128	                if p_start < assistant_start or p_start >= assistant_end:
1129	                    continue
1130	
1131	                # find matching </p>
1132	                for p_end in p_end_positions:
1133	                    if p_end > p_start and p_end <= assistant_end and p_end not in used_end_positions:
1134	                        used_end_positions.add(p_end)
1135	
1136	                        # extract token embeddings between <p> and </p>
1137	                        if p_end > p_start + 1:
1138	                            between_embeddings = hidden_flat[p_start + 1 : p_end]
1139	                            avg_embedding = between_embeddings.mean(dim=0, keepdim=True)
1140	                            qa_queries.append(avg_embedding)
1141	                        break
1142	
1143	            if len(qa_queries) > 0:
1144	                all_query_tokens.append(torch.cat(qa_queries[:2], dim=0)) # only use the first 2 query tokens
1145	            else:
1146	                # this QA has no <p>...</p>, return NaN
1147	                all_query_tokens.append(torch.zeros(1, hidden_dim, device=device))
1148	
1149	            cur_len += rou_len
1150	
1151	        # if grouped_rounds count is less than num_qa, pad with NaN
1152	        while len(all_query_tokens) < num_qa:
1153	            all_query_tokens.append(torch.zeros(1, hidden_dim, device=device))
1154	        all_query_tokens = torch.cat(all_query_tokens, dim=0)
1155	        return all_query_tokens

1159	    def get_query_tokens_id(self, hidden_states, input_ids, num_qa):
1160	        """
1161	        Extract query tokens from hidden_states, grouped by QA pair.
1162	
1163	        Use the special token positions in input_ids directly to divide each assistant
1164	        reply's range, then extract embeddings between <p>...</p> within that range.
1165	
1166	        Difference from get_query_tokens: this function locates assistant ranges based on
1167	        input_ids rather than text, so it is more accurate when extra image tokens, etc.,
1168	        cause text and tokens to be misaligned.
1169	
1170	        Args:
1171	            hidden_states: hidden states of the model's last layer, shape (1, seq_len, hidden_dim)
1172	            input_ids: input token ids, shape (1, seq_len)
1173	            num_qa: number of QA pairs
1174	
1175	        Returns:
1176	            torch.Tensor: concatenated query tokens, shape (total_queries, hidden_dim)
1177	                          same return format as get_query_tokens
1178	        """
1179	        hidden_dim = hidden_states.shape[-1]
1180	        device = hidden_states.device
1181	        tokenizer = self.processor.tokenizer
1182	
1183	        # get ids of special tokens
1184	        p_start_id = self.seg_tokens_ids[0]  # <p>
1185	        p_end_id = self.seg_tokens_ids[1]    # </p>
1186	        im_start_id = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids('<|im_start|>')
1187	        im_end_id = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids('<|im_end|>')
1188	
1189	        input_ids_flat = input_ids[0]  # (seq_len,)
1190	        hidden_flat = hidden_states[0]  # (seq_len, hidden_dim)
1191	
1192	        # find positions of all <p> and </p>
1193	        p_start_positions = (input_ids_flat == p_start_id).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0].tolist()
1194	        p_end_positions = (input_ids_flat == p_end_id).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0].tolist()
1195	
1196	        # find positions of all <|im_start|> and <|im_end|>
1197	        im_start_positions = (input_ids_flat == im_start_id).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0].tolist()
1198	        im_end_positions = (input_ids_flat == im_end_id).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0].tolist()
1199	
1200	        # identify assistant reply ranges
1201	        # strategy: the position of <|im_start|> immediately followed by "assistant" token marks the start of assistant reply
1202	        # the corresponding <|im_end|> marks the end of assistant reply
1203	        assistant_token_id = tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids('assistant')
1204	
1205	        assistant_ranges = []  # [(start, end), ...]
1206	        for im_start_pos in im_start_positions:
1207	            # check whether <|im_start|> is followed by assistant (there may be a newline etc. in between)
1208	            # the usual format is <|im_start|>assistant\n
1209	            check_end = min(im_start_pos + 3, len(input_ids_flat))
1210	            following_ids = input_ids_flat[im_start_pos + 1 : check_end].tolist()
1211	
1212	            if assistant_token_id in following_ids:
1213	                # find the actual start position of the assistant reply (skip "assistant\n")
1214	                assistant_content_start = im_start_pos + 1 + following_ids.index(assistant_token_id) + 1
1215	
1216	                # find the matching <|im_end|> (the first one after assistant_content_start)
1217	                assistant_end = None
1218	                for im_end_pos in im_end_positions:
1219	                    if im_end_pos > assistant_content_start:
1220	                        assistant_end = im_end_pos
1221	                        break
1222	
1223	                if assistant_end is not None:
1224	                    assistant_ranges.append((assistant_content_start, assistant_end))
1225	
1226	        all_query_tokens = []
1227	
1228	        for i in range(num_qa):
1229	            if i >= len(assistant_ranges):
1230	                # assistant_ranges is fewer than num_qa, pad with zero vectors (consistent with get_query_tokens)
1231	                all_query_tokens.append(torch.zeros(1, hidden_dim, device=device))
1232	                continue
1233	
1234	            assistant_start, assistant_end = assistant_ranges[i]
1235	
1236	            # find <p>...</p> within this range
1237	            qa_queries = []
1238	            used_end_positions = set()
1239	
1240	            for p_start in p_start_positions:
1241	                if p_start < assistant_start or p_start >= assistant_end:
1242	                    continue
1243	
1244	                # find matching </p>
1245	                for p_end in p_end_positions:
1246	                    if p_end > p_start and p_end <= assistant_end and p_end not in used_end_positions:
1247	                        used_end_positions.add(p_end)
1248	
1249	                        # extract token embeddings between <p> and </p>
1250	                        if p_end > p_start + 1:
1251	                            between_embeddings = hidden_flat[p_start + 1 : p_end]
1252	                            avg_embedding = between_embeddings.mean(dim=0, keepdim=True)
1253	                            qa_queries.append(avg_embedding)
1254	                        break
1255	
1256	            if len(qa_queries) > 0:
1257	                all_query_tokens.append(torch.cat(qa_queries[:2], dim=0))  # only use the first 2 query tokens
1258	            else:
1259	                # this QA has no <p>...</p>, fill with zero vector (consistent with get_query_tokens)
1260	                all_query_tokens.append(torch.zeros(1, hidden_dim, device=device))
1261	
1262	        all_query_tokens = torch.cat(all_query_tokens, dim=0)
1263	        return all_query_tokens

1625	        Standard LLaVA-style next-token inference: turn 0 injects the point tokens (+ the
1626	        reference RGB frame for the Joint model); each later turn appends the running Q/A
1627	        history and regenerates. No memory / RAG / architectural change.
1628	        """
1629	        qa_level = 'multi_turn_qa_data'
1630	        if qa_level not in pred_qa_data:
1631	            pred_qa_data[qa_level] = []
1632	
1633	        messages = []
1634	        j_mt_qa_results_list = []
1635	
1636	        for j_turn_idx, j_turn_qa_data in enumerate(i_qa_data):
1637	            question = self._get_text(j_turn_qa_data['question'])
1638	            gt_answer = self._get_text(j_turn_qa_data['answer'])
1639	
1640	            # turn 0 carries the point tokens (+ the reference frame); later turns are question-only
1641	            if j_turn_idx == 0:
1642	                input_txt = PART_GLAMM_INSTRUCTION_IMG.format(question=question, point=self.point_token * n_points)
1643	                content = [{'type': 'image', 'image': image_path,

1646	            else:

1648	            messages.append({'role': 'user', 'content': content})
1649	
1650	            # prepare data
1651	            data = self._prepare_messages_data(messages, point_embeds)

1653

1656

1659	            output_text = self.processor.batch_decode(generated_ids, skip_special_tokens=False)[0]
1660	
1661	            # add model response to history for the next round
1662	            messages.append({'role': 'assistant', 'content': [{'type': 'text', 'text': output_text}]})
1663	
1664	            j_mt_qa_results_list.append({

1733	    def _forward_head(self, queries, qa_data, mask_feats, last_flag):
1734	        """Prediction head forward.
1735	
1736	        Args:
1737	            queries (List[Tensor] | Tensor): List of len batch_size,
1738	                each of shape (n_queries_i, d_model). Or tensor of
1739	                shape (batch_size, n_queries, d_model).
1740	            mask_feats (List[Tensor]): of len batch_size,
1741	                each of shape (n_points_i, d_model).
1742	
1743	        Returns:
1744	            Tuple:
1745	                List[Tensor]: Classification predictions of len batch_size,
1746	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_instance_classes + 1).
1747	                List[Tensor] or None: Semantic predictions of len batch_size,
1748	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_semantic_classes + 1).
1749	                List[Tensor]: Confidence scores of len batch_size,
1750	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, 1).
1751	                List[Tensor]: Predicted masks of len batch_size,
1752	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_points_i).
1753	                List[Tensor] or None: Attention masks of len batch_size,
1754	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_points_i).
1755	        """
1756	        pred_scores, pred_masks, attn_masks = [], [], []
1757	
1758	        for i in range(len(queries)):
1759	            norm_query = self.out_norm(queries[i])
1760	    
1761	
1762	            pred_mask = torch.einsum('nd,md->nm', norm_query, mask_feats[i])
1763	                
1764	            if self.attn_mask:
1765	                attn_mask = (pred_mask.sigmoid() < 0.5).bool()
1766	                attn_mask[torch.where(
1767	                    attn_mask.sum(-1) == attn_mask.shape[-1])] = False
1768	                attn_mask = attn_mask.detach()
1769	                attn_masks.append(attn_mask)
1770	            pred_masks.append(pred_mask)
1771	        attn_masks = attn_masks if self.attn_mask else None
1772	        return pred_scores, pred_masks, attn_masks
1773

1781	                shape (batch_size, n_queries, d_model).
1782	            mask_feats (List[Tensor]): of len batch_size,
1783	                each of shape (n_points_i, d_model).
1784	
1785	        Returns:
1786	            Tuple:
1787	                List[Tensor]: Classification predictions of len batch_size,
1788	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_instance_classes + 1).

1790	                    each of shape (n_queries_i, n_semantic_classes + 1).

1799	
1800	        for i in range(len(queries)):

2155	    def get_query_tokens(self, hidden_states, input_ids, text, num_qa):
2156	        """
2157	        Extract query tokens from hidden_states, grouped by QA pair.
2158	
2159	        Following preprocess_chatml's rounds splitting, determine the token range of each
2160	        assistant reply, then extract embeddings between <p>...</p> within that range.
2161	
2162	        Args:
2163	            hidden_states: hidden states of the model's last layer, shape (1, seq_len, hidden_dim)
2164	            input_ids: input token ids, shape (1, seq_len)
2165	            text: full text after apply_chat_template
2166	            num_qa: number of QA pairs
2167	
2168	        Returns:
2169	            list of query tokens, length num_qa, each element is a (num_queries, hidden_dim) tensor
2170	        """
2171	        hidden_dim = hidden_states.shape[-1]
2172	        device = hidden_states.device
2173	        tokenizer = self.processor.tokenizer
2174	
2175	        # get ids of special tokens
2176	        p_start_id = self.seg_tokens_ids[0]  # <p>
2177	        p_end_id = self.seg_tokens_ids[1]    # </p>
2178	
2179	        input_ids_flat = input_ids[0]  # (seq_len,)
2180	        hidden_flat = hidden_states[0]  # (seq_len, hidden_dim)
2181	
2182	        # find positions of all <p> and </p>
2183	        p_start_positions = (input_ids_flat == p_start_id).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0].tolist()
2184	        p_end_positions = (input_ids_flat == p_end_id).nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0].tolist()
2185	
2186	        # follow preprocess_chatml splitting
2187	        conv = get_conv('chatml', qwen_model=self.base_model)
2188	        rounds = [m + conv.seps[0] for m in text.split(conv.seps[0])]
2189	        rounds = rounds[:-1]  # drop the final empty round
2190	
2191	        # grouping: system + user + assistant as one group, then every two (user + assistant) as a group
2192	        if conv.system is None:
2193	            grouped_rounds = [''.join(rounds[i:i + 2]) for i in range(0, len(rounds), 2)]
2194	        else:
2195	            grouped_rounds = [''.join(rounds[:3])] + [''.join(rounds[i:i + 2]) for i in range(3, len(rounds), 2)]
2196	
2197	        # separator: used to split instruction and assistant reply
2198	        sep = conv.seps[0] + conv.roles[1]  # '<|im_end|>\n<|im_start|>assistant\n'
2199	
2200	        all_query_tokens = []
2201	        cur_len = 0
2202	
2203	        for i, rou in enumerate(grouped_rounds):
